name: 0 · The Fool
title: The Fool
imagery: A horned figure dressed in green, part wild spring god and part holy innocent, bursts into the card in mid-stride, carrying a flaming cup and a wand while a bag of coins hangs at his side. A tiger nips at his leg and a crocodile swims beneath him, while a dove, a vulture, a butterfly, grapes and sunflowers swirl through the spiralling ribbons of air. Nothing bites hard enough to stop him: every creature and symbol is part of the overflowing life force he carries into the world.
meaning: In the Thoth deck the Fool is not a naive wanderer but the green god of spring, the breath of Air that exists before anything has taken shape. He stands for pure potential, the zero that contains every number, and for the holy kind of madness that dares to begin without guarantees. This card arrives when life wants you to move from instinct and inspiration rather than calculation. The tiger at his heel and the crocodile below suggest that risk is real, yet the Fool is carried by an enthusiasm so whole that fear cannot grip him. Read it as an invitation to say yes to the unknown, to be playful with your possibilities, and to trust the wild, generous current of your own life.
numerology: Zero is the void that is also fullness, the nothing from which everything springs; in Crowley's thought it is the source behind all numbers rather than the start of a count.
affirmation: I step into the open air of my life and trust the wind to carry me.

ctx.past: Something in your history began with a reckless, beautiful yes. You followed a hunch or a longing before you could explain it, and that burst of green, springtime energy still shapes where you stand today. The wildness of that beginning is part of your story, not a mistake to apologise for.
ctx.present: Right now you are standing in pure possibility, with nothing yet fixed and everything still able to move. The heart of the matter is whether you will let inspiration lead instead of the need for certainty. The breath of Aleph is filling your lungs; your task is simply to step forward on it.
ctx.future: A new cycle is blowing in, fresh as an April wind. Expect an opening that feels unplanned and a little dizzying: a journey, an idea, a chance to reinvent yourself. You do not need to master it in advance; you need to stay curious and light enough to move when it arrives.
ctx.challenge: The Fool's excess is pure scattering: so much enthusiasm that nothing gets grounded, or freedom used as an excuse to dodge every responsibility. The tiger at the ankle is a reminder that consequences exist. The challenge is to keep your wild spirit while still noticing where your feet land.
ctx.advice: Begin before you feel ready, and begin playfully. Choose the option that makes your spirit lift rather than the one that only looks safe on paper. Carry only what you need, keep your sense of humour close, and let yourself be surprised by what grows from a single spontaneous step.
ctx.self: You are in a green, unformed season of yourself, open to everything and committed to nothing yet. This can feel exhilarating or unnerving. Honour it: the part of you that refuses to be pinned down is protecting your capacity to become something genuinely new.
ctx.others: People may see you as unpredictable, inspiring or slightly mad, depending on how comfortable they are with change. Or someone around you is playing the holy fool, breaking rules and stirring the air. Their irreverence may be exactly what loosens a situation that has grown stale.
ctx.hopes: You hope for total freedom, a life where you can follow the wind without asking permission. You may also fear the emptiness of the zero, the moment where nothing is promised. Both feelings point to the same truth: you are ready for a beginning you cannot fully control.
ctx.love: In love the Fool brings spontaneity, laughter and the thrill of not knowing what happens next. A new attraction may arrive out of the blue, or an existing bond may need more play and less planning. Let the relationship breathe, and allow each other room to stay wild.
ctx.work: At work this is the card of the unconventional move: the side project, the leap into freelancing, the idea nobody else has dared to try. Inspiration is high, so harness it with a few simple practical steps. Check the basics before you jump, then trust your originality.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Aleph, the silent letter that is pure breath. Your guides are inviting you to remember that you are a spark of the divine moving freely through the world. Holy foolishness, the willingness to be fully alive without a script, is itself a spiritual practice.
ctx.release: Let go of the need to have everything figured out before you begin. Release the inner critic that calls your enthusiasm naive, and drop the heavy bags of other people's expectations. The Fool travels with almost nothing, and that is exactly why he can move so fast.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath your choices may be a habit of running from commitment and calling it freedom. Or you may be secretly longing for a wild leap you keep postponing. Look at where you are restless, and ask whether you are moving toward life or merely away from discomfort.
ctx.foundation: Underneath this whole situation is raw potential, an impulse that has not yet chosen its form. The root is a spark of desire for something new and unscripted. Everything above it is still flexible, which means the outcome can be shaped by the spirit you bring to it.
ctx.gift: Your gift is an enthusiasm so genuine it disarms fear, both your own and other people's. You can see openings that cautious minds overlook. Hidden help arrives through luck, timing and chance meetings, because life tends to bend toward those who move with this much trust.

name: I · The Magus
title: The Magus
imagery: A swift, winged figure in the likeness of Mercury hangs in a field of light, juggling the tools of creation: wand, cup, sword, disk, along with a pen, a scroll and a winged egg. Behind him rises a great caduceus, and below sits the ape of Thoth, the trickster who echoes and distorts the master's message. The scene shows will and intelligence in constant motion, and the ape is a warning that every true word can also be twisted.
meaning: The Magus is the principle of Mercury: the swift intelligence that turns a single impulse of will into language, plan and action. Where the Fool is pure potential, the Magus is the first deliberate act, the word that sets creation moving. He arrives when you have the skills and resources you need and the moment calls for focused, clever use of them. Communication, learning, negotiation and craft are all highlighted, and so is the responsibility to say what you truly mean. The ape at his feet reminds you that the same quick mind that creates can also deceive, others or yourself, so let your will be honest and your message clear.
numerology: One is the first point, the Word spoken out of the zero; it is will made singular, the beginning of every deliberate creation.
affirmation: My will is clear, my word is true, and my hands know their work.

ctx.past: A deliberate choice set this situation in motion: something you said, learned or skilfully arranged. You used your wits and your voice, and the results of that act are still unfolding. Recognise the power you already showed, because it is a power you can call on again.
ctx.present: Every tool you need is already in your hands, spinning in the air like the Magus's instruments. The heart of the matter is focus: choosing which tool to use and directing your will with precision. This is a moment for clear speech, quick thinking and decisive action.
ctx.future: A period of skilful action is coming, when ideas turn into results through your own effort and ingenuity. Expect messages, contracts, studies or a chance to show what you can do. The more honest and focused your intention, the more cleanly this energy will work for you.
ctx.challenge: The Magus's shadow is the ape of Thoth: cleverness without truth, talk without substance, or juggling so many things that none gets finished. You may be tempted to manipulate or to fool yourself with a convenient story. The challenge is to let your intelligence serve an honest will.
ctx.advice: Name what you want in one clear sentence, then take the first concrete step toward it today. Speak plainly, write it down, and use the skills you already have rather than waiting for more. Choose a single focus and let your quick mind work in its service.
ctx.self: You are feeling capable, sharp and ready to act, perhaps more than you realise. Trust your ability to learn fast and adapt. Your mind is a bright instrument right now; the only question is where you choose to point it.
ctx.others: Others see you as articulate, resourceful and persuasive, the person who can make things happen. Or someone in your circle is a skilled communicator or dealmaker. Listen closely to what they say and how they say it, and check whether their words and actions match.
ctx.hopes: You hope to prove that your ideas and talents can shape real outcomes. You may also fear being seen as a fraud, or being outwitted by someone cleverer. Both concerns ask the same thing of you: say what you mean, and back it with genuine skill.
ctx.love: In love the Magus favours honest, lively communication and intentional courtship. Say what you feel rather than hinting at it. In a relationship, this card asks whether your words and your actions agree, and invites you both to create something together on purpose.
ctx.work: At work this is a strong card for pitching, writing, teaching, negotiating, coding, trading or any craft that rewards agility. Your skills are ready to be used, and a well-timed message can open doors. Read the small print and keep your dealings transparent.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Beth, the house, and through Mercury, messenger of the gods. Your guides remind you that your true Will is sacred, and that words carry real power. Spiritual growth now comes through mindful speech, study and conscious creation.
ctx.release: Release the habit of overthinking, explaining and second-guessing until the moment for action has passed. Let go of half-truths you tell to keep the peace. A clean, simple message will serve you better than any amount of clever spinning.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a talent you underuse because you doubt its worth, or a part of you that enjoys being clever more than being truthful. Notice where your words drift away from what you actually feel. That gap is where the ape of Thoth makes mischief.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies an act of will: a decision, a message or a plan that launched everything else. The situation grows from intelligence and intention. Understanding exactly what was meant at the start will help you steer what happens next.
ctx.gift: Your gift is a nimble, inventive mind and the ability to turn ideas into reality. You learn quickly, find the right words and spot connections others miss. Hidden help comes through a conversation, a book or a timely message that sharpens your direction.

name: II · The Priestess
title: The Priestess
imagery: A luminous goddess sits enthroned within a shimmering veil of light, her arms raised to form a great crescent, with a hunter's bow resting across her knees. At her feet lie crystals, seeds, fruits and flowers, the raw promise of life waiting to unfold, and a small camel wanders at the very bottom of the card. The veil is not a wall but a living web of light, and the camel recalls the long, solitary desert crossing that leads from the human to the divine.
meaning: The Priestess is the Moon in her purest aspect: a silver thread linking your everyday self with the deepest source of your being. In the Thoth deck she is the virgin huntress Artemis, self-contained and free, whose bow is the tension of intuition ready to fly. She asks you to listen inward, to trust knowledge that arrives as feeling, image or dream rather than argument. Nothing needs to be forced here; insight comes when you are still and receptive. This card often appears when the answer you seek is already within you, quietly waiting behind a veil that only patience and honesty can part.
numerology: Two is the first reflection, the mirror in which the one becomes aware of itself; here it is receptivity, polarity and the knowing that comes through stillness.
affirmation: In stillness I hear the truth that has always lived within me.

ctx.past: Your intuition was speaking long before this situation took shape, perhaps through a dream, a gut feeling or a quiet sense of knowing. Some of the roots lie in a time when you were inward, private or listening carefully. What you sensed then still holds a key to now.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter lies beneath the surface, not yet fully spoken or seen. This is a time to observe, reflect and feel rather than push for answers. Trust the subtle signals you are receiving, because the veil is thinner than it looks.
ctx.future: A period of deepening intuition and inner clarity is coming. Something hidden may reveal itself gradually, or you may find yourself drawn to quieter, more contemplative ways of living. Let insight ripen in its own time, like the fruits resting at the Priestess's feet.
ctx.challenge: The Priestess's excess is withdrawal: retreating so far into your inner world that you become distant, secretive or passive. You may be waiting for perfect certainty before acting. The challenge is to honour your intuition while still letting it touch the waking world.
ctx.advice: Make space for silence. Journal, meditate, walk alone or simply sleep on the question before you decide. Pay attention to dreams, coincidences and the first feeling that arises before your mind starts arguing. Act only once you feel the bowstring of intuition pull taut.
ctx.self: You are in a receptive, perceptive state, more tuned in to undercurrents than usual. You may prefer to keep your thoughts to yourself for now, and that is fine. Your inner knowing is a quiet authority; trust it even if you cannot yet explain it.
ctx.others: Others may find you mysterious or hard to read, sensing depth they cannot quite reach. Or someone around you holds knowledge they are not ready to share. Approach them gently; trust and patience will reveal more than direct questioning.
ctx.hopes: You hope for clarity, for some sign that you are on the right path. You may also fear what lies behind the veil, worried that the truth will ask something of you. Remember that the Priestess's light is gentle; revelation here unfolds kindly.
ctx.love: In love the Priestess brings depth, emotional intuition and a bond that runs deeper than words. There may be unspoken feelings on one side or both. Give each other space to be whole on your own, and listen for what is felt rather than only what is said.
ctx.work: At work this card favours research, counselling, healing, the arts, or any role that needs discretion and sensitivity. Keep plans confidential until they are ready. If a decision feels murky, gather information quietly and let your instincts guide the final call.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Gimel, the camel, and the Moon's silver path across the desert of the mind. Your guides invite you into direct inner communion, without intermediaries. Practices of stillness, dreamwork and lunar ritual of a gentle kind will open you further.
ctx.release: Let go of the need to have every answer explained in logical terms. Release the noise of other people's opinions that drowns out your own inner voice. Some things are meant to be felt before they are understood.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the surface may be an intuition you keep overriding because it is inconvenient. Or you may be hiding behind mystery to avoid being truly seen. Ask what you already know but have not admitted, even to yourself.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this matter lies something unseen: a feeling, a secret or an intuition that has been shaping events quietly. The real cause is not on the surface. Look inward and to the subtle currents, and the structure of the situation will make sense.
ctx.gift: Your gift is deep perception, the ability to sense truth beneath appearances. You can hold space for mystery without panicking. Hidden help arrives through dreams, synchronicities and the quiet voice that speaks most clearly when you stop asking so loudly.

name: III · The Empress
title: The Empress
imagery: A crowned queen sits enthroned in soft blues and greens, her arms and body forming the alchemical sign of salt, a lotus in one hand. At her feet a pelican feeds its young from its own breast, and beside her rests a shield bearing a white double-headed eagle, while sparrows, doves, bees and a waxing moon fill the space around her. The pelican shows self-giving love, the doves and sparrows are sacred to Venus, and the arch behind her is the gateway through which all life enters the world.
meaning: The Empress is Venus on the Tree of Life, the door through which spirit pours into form. She is love in its most generous, creative sense: the force that makes gardens bloom, children grow, art take shape and friendships deepen. In the Thoth tradition she is the feminine principle in harmony with the active masculine of the Emperor, and her presence signals fertility on every level. When she appears, something is ready to be nourished into fullness, whether a project, a relationship or your own sense of beauty and worth. She asks you to receive pleasure without guilt, to tend what you love patiently, and to trust that abundance is a natural state rather than a reward you must earn.
numerology: Three is the first birth, the union of one and two producing a child; it is creativity, growth and the overflowing of love into form.
affirmation: I am a gateway for love, and everything I tend with care grows lush and strong.

ctx.past: This situation grew from a season of fertility and care, when something was lovingly nurtured into being. Perhaps you were creative, generous or deeply connected to someone. The warmth of that time is still feeding what you have now.
ctx.present: Life is ripening around you. The heart of the matter is growth: a project, relationship or part of yourself that is ready to flourish if you keep tending it. Enjoy your senses, your surroundings and the pleasure of making something beautiful.
ctx.future: Abundance is on its way: a creative birth, a period of comfort and plenty, or a relationship blossoming. Expect things to grow at a natural pace, neither rushed nor stalled. Keep watering what matters and the harvest will be generous.
ctx.challenge: The Empress's excess is smothering or overindulgence: giving so much that you empty yourself like the pelican, or sinking into comfort until nothing moves. You may be nurturing everyone except yourself. The challenge is to let love flow in both directions.
ctx.advice: Nourish what you want to grow. Give time, attention and tenderness to your body, your home, your art or your relationships. Surround yourself with beauty and allow yourself pleasure. Growth comes now through care and patience rather than force.
ctx.self: You are feeling, or ready to feel, fertile and abundant, full of creative and loving energy. Your warmth is magnetic. Let yourself be both giver and receiver, and treat your own needs with the same devotion you give to others.
ctx.others: Others see you as caring, beautiful in spirit and a source of comfort. Or a nurturing figure, often a mother, mentor or generous friend, is a strong presence in your environment. Their support is real; let yourself lean on it.
ctx.hopes: You hope for love, beauty, security and creative fulfilment, perhaps for a family or a home that feels truly yours. You may also fear scarcity, or that you will give too much and be left with nothing. The Empress answers: love multiplies when it is shared wisely.
ctx.love: This is one of the most loving cards in the deck. It brings affection, sensuality, commitment and sometimes the wish for a family. A relationship can deepen into real partnership now. Offer and receive tenderness openly, and enjoy each other.
ctx.work: At work the Empress favours creative fields, design, hospitality, care, gardening and anything that grows over time. Projects that you nurture patiently will prosper. Money can flow more easily when you work with what you love rather than against it.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Daleth, the door, and through Venus, the star of love. Your guides remind you that the physical world is sacred and that love is a spiritual force. Gratitude, beauty and time in nature are powerful forms of prayer now.
ctx.release: Release the belief that you must struggle or sacrifice to deserve good things. Let go of guilt around rest and pleasure, and of relationships where you give endlessly without receiving. Love that drains you is asking to be rebalanced.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a pattern of over-giving that quietly breeds resentment, or a creative longing you have kept in the shade. Ask whether you allow yourself to be nurtured as fully as you nurture others. What wants to be born in you?
ctx.foundation: At the root lies love: a bond, a creative desire or a deep wish to nurture. The whole situation grows from fertile ground. Whatever problems appear on the surface, the foundation is rich and capable of sustaining real growth.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the power to make things flourish through warmth and care. You bring beauty and comfort wherever you go. Hidden help arrives through nature, friends, mothers or mentors, and through the simple pleasures that refill your cup.

name: IV · The Emperor
title: The Emperor
imagery: A crowned king in flame-red sits in profile with his legs crossed and his arms and head forming a triangle above a cross, the alchemical sign of sulphur. Wild Himalayan rams leap behind him and rest at his feet, a lamb carrying a banner lies below, and his shield bears a red double-headed eagle crowned with the sun. The rams speak of Aries' bold drive, the lamb of the gentle side of true power, and the sulphur pose of fiery, active energy held in steady form.
meaning: The Emperor is the fire of Aries brought under command: raw energy shaped into leadership, structure and decisive action. In the Thoth deck he is the active masculine partner of the Empress, the father who protects and organises what love has created. He represents the ability to take charge, set boundaries, make plans and carry them through. When he appears, life asks you to step up and own your authority, to build something that can last, and to govern your own impulses with confidence. Crowley notes that such power must keep renewing itself or it hardens into tyranny, so the best Emperor leads with initiative and fairness, not mere control.
numerology: Four is the square and the first solid form, the number of order and law; it gives the fire of creation a structure to stand on.
affirmation: I lead my life with courage, clarity and steady command.

ctx.past: This situation was built by a decisive act of leadership, perhaps your own, perhaps that of a strong figure in your life. Structures, rules or plans were laid down that still shape things today. Recognise both the security and the limits that this foundation created.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter is authority and order. You are being asked to take charge, set clear boundaries and make decisions rather than waiting for someone else. Your energy is strong right now; give it a shape and a direction.
ctx.future: A time of stability, achievement and increased responsibility is approaching. You may find yourself in a leadership role or building something solid and lasting. The fiery start of a new cycle is available if you meet it with discipline and vision.
ctx.challenge: The Emperor's shadow is rigidity and domination: clinging to control, refusing to adapt, or letting the ram's aggression run the show. Power that never renews itself turns stale. The challenge is to lead with strength while staying open to change and to other voices.
ctx.advice: Take command of the situation. Make a plan, set firm boundaries and follow through with confidence. Organise your time, your money or your space so that your energy can flow productively. Be the steady, protective presence you would want to follow.
ctx.self: You see yourself as capable and in charge, or you are being called to become so. Trust your capacity to lead, decide and protect. You do not need anyone's permission to take responsibility for your own life.
ctx.others: Others see you as strong, reliable and authoritative, someone who gets things done. Or a powerful figure, a boss, parent or official, is shaping your environment. Engage with them directly and respectfully, and hold your own ground.
ctx.hopes: You hope for security, recognition and the freedom that comes from being in control of your own life. You may also fear being dominated or losing control. Both point toward the same need: a structure that supports you instead of confining you.
ctx.love: In love the Emperor brings commitment, loyalty and protectiveness. A relationship may become more stable and defined, with clear agreements. Watch for power struggles, and make sure that strength in the partnership is shared rather than held by one person alone.
ctx.work: At work this is a powerful card for leadership, entrepreneurship, management and long-term planning. Your initiative will be noticed. Set up systems, budgets and clear goals; this is a time to build an empire one well-placed stone at a time.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through the fire of Aries and the letter Tzaddi, which Crowley gave to this card. Your guides remind you that self-mastery is a sacred path. Ruling yourself with courage and fairness is how you honour your true Will.
ctx.release: Release the need to control every detail and every person. Let go of outdated rules that no longer serve, and of anger that has turned into stubbornness. True authority is secure enough to bend when it must.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a fear of vulnerability dressed up as strength, or an inner tyrant who criticises you mercilessly. You may also be avoiding your own power because leadership feels like a burden. Ask where you could govern yourself more kindly.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a need for order, safety or direction. The whole situation rests on how power and responsibility are held. Strengthen the foundation by making the structure fair, clear and alive rather than merely rigid.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the ability to take raw energy and make something lasting from it. You can organise, protect and lead. Hidden help comes through mentors, institutions or your own capacity to stay steady when others waver.

name: V · The Hierophant
title: The Hierophant
imagery: A robed teacher sits enthroned upon a bull, flanked by elephants and framed by the four sacred beasts in the corners, with a window of light behind him. On his breast a pentagram holds a dancing child, and before him stands a woman girded with a sword. The bull and elephants embody Taurus' patient strength, while the child within the star shows that the teaching itself is being reborn for a new age.
meaning: The Hierophant is the revealer of mysteries, the one who carries spiritual teaching from the inner world into the outer. In the Thoth deck he belongs to Taurus, slow and enduring, and he represents wisdom that has been earned over time. Yet Crowley's Hierophant is not a stern guardian of old dogma: the child on his breast signals that tradition is being renewed, that the living spirit must keep breaking through the forms. This card can point to a teacher, a course of study, an initiation or a commitment, and also to the inner voice that guides you. It asks you to learn patiently, to honour what is genuinely wise in tradition, and to let your own understanding grow beyond it.
numerology: Five is the pentagram, spirit crowning the four elements; it is the human being awake within structure, the bridge between law and living experience.
affirmation: I learn from the wisdom of the ages and let it come alive in me.

ctx.past: Your roots here lie in teaching, tradition or a formative commitment: a school, a faith, a family code or a mentor whose words stayed with you. Those lessons laid down patterns you still follow. Some may still serve you, and some may be ready to be updated.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter is learning and meaning. You may be studying, seeking guidance or being asked to commit to a path. Listen for the inner teacher as well as the outer one, and give yourself time to understand rather than rushing.
ctx.future: An initiation or a lesson is approaching: a course, a mentor, a ceremony or a decision that will deepen your understanding. Expect growth that comes steadily rather than overnight. What you learn now will form a solid part of your future.
ctx.challenge: The Hierophant's excess is stubbornness and conformity: holding to rules simply because they are old, or waiting for an authority to tell you what to think. The bull can be immovable. The challenge is to respect tradition while keeping your own inner voice alive.
ctx.advice: Seek out a good teacher, a trusted source or a structured practice, and give it patient commitment. Ask real questions and be willing to sit with the answers. At the same time, test every teaching against your own experience before you adopt it.
ctx.self: You are in the role of student, teacher or seeker, perhaps all three. You value meaning and integrity. Trust that your patient, steady approach will lead to genuine understanding, and that your own insight is worth sharing.
ctx.others: Others see you as wise, dependable and principled, someone they come to for guidance. Or a mentor, institution or community is an important influence. Their structure can support you, as long as it leaves room for your individuality.
ctx.hopes: You hope to find meaning, a teacher or a path that makes sense of your life. You may also fear being trapped by expectations or losing yourself in a group. The Hierophant shows that true belonging includes your own voice.
ctx.love: In love this card points to commitment, shared values and the desire for a relationship with real foundations. It can suggest marriage, vows or a bond strengthened by common beliefs. Talk openly about what each of you holds sacred.
ctx.work: At work the Hierophant favours education, training, mentoring, established institutions and long-term projects. Learn the system thoroughly before you try to change it, and seek out someone experienced who can show you its unwritten rules. Slow, consistent effort will build credibility and lasting value.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Vav, the nail that joins heaven and earth. Your guides suggest that a new kind of spiritual understanding is being born in you, one that honours the old wisdom but speaks in your own voice. Listen to your inner teacher.
ctx.release: Release beliefs you inherited but never examined, and the need for external approval of your spiritual or personal choices. Let go of guilt rooted in outdated rules. Keep what is wise and lay the rest down gently.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a reliance on authority that keeps you from trusting yourself, or a quiet rebellion you have not admitted. You might also hold a wisdom you are hesitant to teach. Ask whose voice is really speaking when you say what you should do.
ctx.foundation: At the root lie values, beliefs or a framework that has shaped everything above it. Understanding the principles you are operating from will clarify the whole situation. The question is whether that framework is still alive or merely habitual.
ctx.gift: Your gift is patience and the ability to learn deeply and pass wisdom on. You can hold a steady centre in changing times. Hidden help comes through teachers, elders, books and the quiet inner voice that grows clearer the more you listen.

name: VI · The Lovers
title: The Lovers
imagery: A hooded figure with outstretched arms presides over the sacred marriage of a dark crowned king and a fair crowned queen, who exchange symbols of their natures. Above them a blindfolded Cupid draws his bow, and around them gather a dark woman and a fair one, two children, a lion and an eagle, and a winged egg wrapped by a serpent. Everything in the card comes in pairs, showing that opposites are drawn together so that something new can be born from their union.
meaning: In the Thoth deck the Lovers, sometimes called the Brothers, is the first stage of an inner alchemy: the meeting and marriage of opposites. It belongs to Gemini, the twins, and it speaks of attraction, communication and the fertile tension between two forces. Romance is certainly part of its meaning, but at heart this card is about integration, bringing together masculine and feminine, light and dark, reason and feeling within yourself. It may also mark an important choice, one that reveals what you truly love. Cupid's arrow suggests that inspiration strikes when you stop analysing and let your heart and Will align.
numerology: Six is harmony and balance, the meeting of two triangles; it is the number of beauty created when opposites are reconciled.
affirmation: I welcome the meeting of opposites in me and choose what my heart truly loves.

ctx.past: This situation was shaped by a meeting or a choice: a relationship that began, an alliance formed or a path you selected over another. Two forces came together and something new emerged. That union, and the decision behind it, still influences you.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter is union and choice. Two people, two options or two sides of yourself are drawn together, and the question is how they can work as one. Listen to what you genuinely love, not only to what seems logical.
ctx.future: A meaningful connection or important decision is coming. Expect attraction, partnership or a realisation that brings opposing parts of your life into harmony. Something fertile may grow from this joining if you approach it with honesty.
ctx.challenge: The Lovers' shadow is division and indecision: being torn between options, projecting your inner conflict onto a partner, or choosing with the head while the heart says otherwise. The twins can pull apart as well as together. The challenge is to choose wholeheartedly.
ctx.advice: Bring both sides to the table. Talk honestly, listen fully and look for the third way that honours each force. If a choice is required, make it from love and true Will rather than fear. Commit to the path that makes you feel whole.
ctx.self: You are in a season of attraction and integration, aware of different sides of yourself wanting to meet. Embrace both your light and your darkness. You become more whole, and more magnetic, when you stop rejecting any part of who you are.
ctx.others: Others may see you as part of a pair, or as someone on the verge of a significant choice. A partner, collaborator or twin-like figure may be prominent in your environment. Their difference from you is exactly what makes the alliance powerful.
ctx.hopes: You hope for a deep, meaningful union, with another person or within yourself. You may also fear choosing wrongly or losing yourself in a relationship. Remember that true union strengthens both partners rather than erasing one of them.
ctx.love: This is a strong card for love: attraction, chemistry, meaningful conversation and the possibility of commitment. Existing relationships can deepen through honest exchange. It also invites you to value your differences, since they are what spark the alchemy between you.
ctx.work: At work the Lovers point to partnerships, collaborations and decisions about direction. Choose projects and colleagues that genuinely inspire you. Combining two very different skills or ideas can produce something original and valuable, so look for the partner whose strengths complement yours.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Zayin, the sword that divides so that union can happen consciously. Your guides invite you into inner alchemy, the sacred marriage of all your opposites. The winged egg reminds you that something new is being conceived within you.
ctx.release: Release the habit of seeing life in strict either-or terms. Let go of relationships, ideas or commitments you keep only out of duty, and the fear of disappointing others by following your heart. Choose clearly and the tension eases.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a part of yourself you project onto others, admiring or resenting in them what you have not yet claimed. Or you may be avoiding a choice by keeping all options open. Ask what you truly desire beneath the surface.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a meeting of two forces, whether a relationship, a partnership or an inner tension. The whole situation grows from how these opposites relate. When they are reconciled, the foundation becomes unusually strong.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the ability to connect, to build bridges and to hold two truths at once. You can create harmony where others see only conflict. Hidden help comes through partnership, honest conversation and the inspiration of love.

name: VII · The Chariot
title: The Chariot
imagery: A charioteer clad in amber armour sits cross-legged within a canopied chariot, holding a glowing cup before him like a sacred treasure, his helmet crowned with a crab. Four sphinxes, each blending the bull, lion, eagle and human, draw the vehicle, and its wheels are bright red with motion. He does not hold the reins at all: the chariot moves by the harmony of its forces, while the warrior's true task is to carry and protect the grail.
meaning: The Thoth Chariot belongs to Cancer, the crab, whose hard shell protects a tender heart. The charioteer is a guardian of something holy, carrying the grail of life through the world, and his victory comes from inner stillness rather than force. This card speaks of momentum, success and the ability to move forward with protection around you. It asks you to know what you are carrying, your purpose, your values, your heart, and to let that be the centre of your action. When your inner forces are aligned, you do not need to grip the reins; the chariot moves of its own accord, and triumph follows.
numerology: Seven is a number of victory and of testing; it is the moment when established form is set in motion toward a new goal.
affirmation: I carry what is sacred to me and move forward with calm, unstoppable strength.

ctx.past: This situation began with a forward movement: a decision to go, a challenge you met or a goal you pursued with determination. You protected what mattered to you and kept going. The momentum of that victory still carries you.
ctx.present: You are in motion right now, and the heart of the matter is direction and purpose. Know what you are carrying and why. If your inner forces are aligned, progress will feel surprisingly smooth; if they pull in different directions, pause and realign.
ctx.future: Success and forward progress are coming. Expect travel, a breakthrough or a victory that comes from steady commitment. Keep your heart protected and your aim clear, and the road ahead will open. A move, a journey or a hard-won win may be part of what arrives.
ctx.challenge: The Chariot's shadow is the armour becoming a prison: defensiveness, emotional shutdown or relentless drive that loses sight of its purpose. You may be forcing things instead of trusting alignment. The challenge is to keep moving without hardening your heart.
ctx.advice: Clarify what you are fighting for, then commit to it fully. Protect your energy and your boundaries, but stay emotionally open. Let your actions flow from a calm centre rather than tight control, and keep moving steadily toward your goal.
ctx.self: You see yourself as determined, protective and on a mission. You have the strength to keep going when others falter. Remember that your sensitivity is part of your power; it tells you what is worth carrying.
ctx.others: Others see you as driven and capable, perhaps a little guarded. Or someone around you is on the move, focused and protective of their own goals. Respect their momentum and look for ways to travel in the same direction.
ctx.hopes: You hope for victory, progress and the sense of being in charge of your direction. You may also fear losing control or being left exposed. The Chariot suggests that real security comes from inner alignment more than from heavier armour.
ctx.love: In love the Chariot brings momentum and protection: a relationship moving forward, perhaps a move together or a shared goal. It can also show one partner guarding their heart. Let your devotion be visible, and steer together rather than pulling against each other.
ctx.work: At work this is a card of progress, ambition and well-earned success. Projects gain speed when you focus and protect your time. Travel or relocation for work is possible. Stay disciplined, and keep the purpose of your work in sight.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Cheth, the fence or enclosure, and through Cancer's protective shell. Your guides remind you that you are a carrier of something sacred. Your spiritual task is to keep that light safe while bringing it boldly into the world.
ctx.release: Release the need to control every rein and every outcome. Let go of defensive habits that keep love out along with harm. You can afford to soften the armour a little; your inner strength is real.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be emotional vulnerability you keep well armoured, or a restless drive that keeps you from feeling what you feel. Ask what exactly you are protecting, and whether it still needs so much defence.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a strong sense of purpose and a need to protect something precious. The situation is built on motion and determination. When the purpose is clear, the whole structure becomes powerful and coherent.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the ability to keep moving forward with grace and strength, holding your centre while the world rushes past. You protect what is sacred. Hidden help comes from inner alignment and from the momentum you have already built.

name: XI · Lust
title: Lust
imagery: A radiant woman rides joyfully upon a many-headed lion-beast, leaning back in delight as she lifts a blazing grail high above her head. The reins she holds are loose, for she guides the beast through union and joy rather than force, and behind her the background is alive with streams of light and the outlines of new forms waiting to be born. The lion is raw, untamed life energy, and the cup of fire is that energy offered up, turned into creative ecstasy.
meaning: Crowley renamed Strength as Lust to show that the deepest power is not restraint but joyful, wholehearted engagement with life. This is the fire of Leo: courage, vitality and the ecstasy of being fully alive. The woman does not subdue the beast; she rides it in partnership, and their union generates a creative energy that can transform the world. In a reading Lust speaks of passion for a person, a project or life itself, of the strength that arrives when you stop fighting your own nature, and of the confidence to follow your true Will. It is a card of the new Aeon of Horus, where the child of joy replaces the old fear of the instincts, so let your vitality become a sacred and creative force.
numerology: Eleven is the number of magick in Crowley's system, one beyond ten, the leap outside ordinary limits; it is energy that expands and transforms.
affirmation: I ride my passion with joy, and my vitality becomes a creative fire.

ctx.past: A wave of passion or courage set this situation in motion. You followed a strong desire, took a bold risk or embraced something with your whole heart. That fiery beginning still gives the situation its energy and warmth.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter is vitality and passion. You have access to tremendous energy right now, and the question is whether you will ride it or resist it. Trust your strength and let enthusiasm, rather than fear, steer your choices.
ctx.future: A season of renewed energy, confidence and creative joy is coming. Expect a passion to ignite, whether for a person, a project or life itself. You will find you are stronger and braver than you thought.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of Lust is excess: energy that burns without direction, appetites that run the show, or intensity that overwhelms others. The beast can bolt as well as dance. The challenge is to keep joy and passion joined to a clear, conscious will.
ctx.advice: Throw your whole self into what you love. Act with courage and enthusiasm, take pleasure in the process and let your natural instincts guide you. Treat your passion as sacred energy, and channel it into creating something real.
ctx.self: You are feeling, or ready to feel, vibrant, confident and alive in your body and spirit. Your natural magnetism is strong. Stop apologising for your intensity; it is a gift when you let it flow with purpose.
ctx.others: Others see you as passionate, bold and inspiring, perhaps a little untamed. Or someone around you is radiating charisma and energy that is hard to ignore. Let their fire inspire you, while staying true to your own direction.
ctx.hopes: You hope to live boldly, love fiercely and feel truly alive. You may also fear your own intensity or worry about losing control. Lust reminds you that joyful strength and wisdom can travel together, and that the beast becomes a partner once you stop fearing it.
ctx.love: In love this card brings chemistry, warmth and deep attraction. A relationship can be playful, sensual and full of mutual delight. Passion thrives on honesty and enthusiasm, so share what excites you and let affection be generous and celebratory.
ctx.work: At work Lust brings drive, creativity and the courage to take on big challenges. You are most successful now when you love what you do. Pursue projects that set you on fire, and let your enthusiasm carry others along with you.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Teth, the serpent, and the solar fire of Leo. Your guides invite you to see your life force as holy, not something to be ashamed of. In the spirit of the new Aeon, joy and freedom are themselves paths to the divine.
ctx.release: Release shame about your desires, your body or your enthusiasm. Let go of the belief that strength means suppressing your nature. True power comes through partnership with your instincts, not war against them. Loosen your grip on the reins and let joy lead for a while.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a passion you have suppressed for so long that it has turned into frustration or restlessness. Or you may be using intensity to avoid deeper feelings. Ask what you truly desire, and whether you are allowing yourself to pursue it.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies raw life energy, desire and courage. The whole situation grows from passion, which can be harnessed to create something remarkable. Understand what fires you up and you understand what drives this matter.
ctx.gift: Your gift is radiant vitality and the courage to engage fully with life. You inspire others simply by being so alive. Hidden help arrives through your own enthusiasm, which opens doors and gives you strength to meet any challenge.

name: IX · The Hermit
title: The Hermit
imagery: A cloaked and bent figure, seen from above, holds out a lantern whose light is a small sun, set amid a field of ripe wheat. Before him floats a winged egg encircled by a serpent, a twisting seed-like form of life spirals nearby, and a three-headed hound follows obediently at his heels. The wheat and the seed speak of Virgo's fertile earth and the hidden spark of life, while the tamed hound shows that the wise one has mastered his fears.
meaning: The Hermit in the Thoth deck is the bearer of the secret seed of life, the wise one who carries light quietly into dark places. He belongs to Virgo, the earth sign of harvest and discernment, and to the letter Yod, the small flame from which every other letter grows. His solitude is not loneliness but concentration: he has withdrawn to tend the inner light until it is strong enough to illuminate the world. This card often appears when you need time alone to think, study or heal, or when your wisdom is ready to guide others. It promises that the light you cultivate in silence will become a seed of renewal for yourself and those around you.
numerology: Nine is the last single digit, the completion that contains all that came before; it is wisdom, ripeness and the seed that will start the next cycle.
affirmation: I tend my inner light, and it shines the way for me and for others.

ctx.past: This situation has roots in a period of withdrawal, study or reflection. You took time to think, perhaps by choice, perhaps by necessity. The wisdom you gathered then quietly shapes how you see things now.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter calls for quiet and reflection. Step back from the noise, consult your own inner light and examine the details carefully. The answer you need will come from within, not from the crowd.
ctx.future: A time of introspection and inner growth is coming, which will ripen into clarity and wisdom. You may seek solitude, take up study or find a guide. What looks like a pause is actually a seed being planted for something new.
ctx.challenge: The Hermit's excess is isolation and overanalysis: shutting yourself away too long, or examining every detail until you cannot act. The lantern can become a hiding place. The challenge is to share your light rather than guarding it forever.
ctx.advice: Make time for solitude and focused thought. Simplify, look closely at what matters and trust your own judgment. Seek out knowledge or a wise guide if you need one, and then let your insights take practical form.
ctx.self: You see yourself as independent, thoughtful and quietly capable. You may be craving space to reflect. Honour that need without guilt; your careful, discerning mind is one of your greatest strengths right now, and it works best when it has room to breathe.
ctx.others: Others see you as wise, reserved and perhaps a little distant. Or a mentor, therapist or quiet expert is important in your environment. Their measured perspective can illuminate what you have been missing, so seek them out and listen more than you speak.
ctx.hopes: You hope for clarity, peace and a deeper understanding of yourself. You may also fear loneliness or being misunderstood. The Hermit shows that true solitude is full of presence, and that your light attracts kindred spirits.
ctx.love: In love the Hermit asks for depth over excitement. You may need some space, or a relationship may benefit from quiet, thoughtful conversation. Partners who honour each other's independence will grow closer. If single, time alone now prepares you for a truer connection.
ctx.work: At work this card favours research, analysis, writing, craftsmanship and any role that requires expertise and care. Attention to detail will pay off. Working independently or consulting may suit you well; let your knowledge speak for itself.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Yod, the tiny flame that is the seed of all creation. Your guides invite you into contemplation and retreat. The light you seek is already within you, small and bright, and it grows each time you turn toward it.
ctx.release: Release the need for constant input, distraction and approval. Let go of perfectionism that keeps you endlessly checking details. Some things are already clear enough to act on now, and the light you carry is bright enough to take the next step by.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a habit of withdrawing to avoid conflict or vulnerability, or a fear that your wisdom is not enough. You may also be ignoring the guidance you already hold. Ask whether your solitude is nourishing you or protecting you from life.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a need for inner truth and understanding. The situation grows from careful thought, quiet growth or a search for meaning. Strengthen it by trusting what you discover in your own reflection.
ctx.gift: Your gift is quiet wisdom and the ability to see what others overlook. Your light, though small, can guide many. Hidden help comes through solitude, study, nature and the voice of your own deeper self.

name: X · Fortune
title: Fortune
imagery: A great ten-spoked wheel spins against a violet sky crackling with lightning and scattered stars. Three figures ride it: a crowned sphinx with a sword sits at the top, a jackal-headed figure climbs up one side and a crocodile-like creature tumbles down the other. They represent the three forces that keep all things moving, balance, rising energy and falling inertia, and the storm of light around them shows a universe in constant, electrifying motion.
meaning: Fortune is the card of Jupiter, the great benefic, and of the letter Kaph, the open palm. In the Thoth tradition it shows the universe as a ceaseless whirl of energy in which nothing stays still, and the three figures on the wheel represent the forces that drive every change. This card announces a turning point: luck shifting, circumstances moving, a new phase beginning. Because it belongs to Jupiter, the change tends toward growth and opportunity, especially if you ride the motion rather than clinging to what was. Fortune asks you to stay alert, flexible and ready to act when the wheel brings your moment around.
numerology: Ten is completion and return to one on a new level; it is the cycle fulfilled and the wheel ready to turn again.
affirmation: I move with the turning of the wheel and welcome the opportunities it brings.

ctx.past: A turning point shaped this situation: a stroke of luck, an unexpected change or the end of one cycle and the start of another. Circumstances shifted in ways you could not have planned. That turn of the wheel still sets the stage for now.
ctx.present: The wheel is turning right now. The heart of the matter is change, and the question is whether you can move with it rather than resisting. Stay flexible and alert; opportunities are arriving that may not stay for long.
ctx.future: A significant shift is coming, likely bringing growth, luck or new opportunities. Expect events to speed up and circumstances to rearrange themselves. Be ready to seize the moment when it comes around, because Jupiter's turns reward those who act while the door is open.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of Fortune is feeling at the mercy of events, or riding the wheel so frantically that you lose your centre. You may be clinging to something that has already passed, or waiting for luck instead of acting. The challenge is to find stillness within the motion.
ctx.advice: Go with the flow of change. Say yes to opportunities, stay adaptable and keep your eyes open for openings. Remember that what goes down also comes up, and use this moment to position yourself well for the next turn.
ctx.self: You are in a period of change, perhaps feeling both excited and unsettled. Trust your ability to adapt. You do not need to control the wheel; you only need to find your balance as it turns.
ctx.others: Others may see you as someone whose life is changing quickly, or as lucky and well positioned. Or shifting circumstances around you are creating movement for everyone. Stay connected, since new opportunities often arrive through other people now.
ctx.hopes: You hope for a lucky break, a change of fortune or relief from a stuck situation. You may also fear sudden change or loss of stability. Fortune reminds you that cycles keep turning, and this turn favours growth.
ctx.love: In love Fortune brings change and movement: a fated meeting, a new stage in a relationship or a reconnection with someone from the past. It favours openness and trust in timing. If things feel uncertain, know that the wheel is already moving toward something new.
ctx.work: At work this card signals opportunity, expansion and changing conditions. A promotion, a new contract or a lucky opening may appear. Stay alert to timing, act decisively when the moment comes and avoid over-committing to any one fixed plan.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Kaph, the open hand, and generous Jupiter. Your guides remind you that life is a dance of cycles and that each turn carries lessons. Trust the larger pattern even when you cannot yet see it.
ctx.release: Release the need for everything to stay the same. Let go of resentment about past turns of fate and of the belief that luck happens only to other people. Open hands can receive what the wheel brings.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a habit of blaming fate rather than taking action, or an addiction to excitement and change. Ask whether you are participating in your life or merely watching it turn. Your choices are part of the wheel too.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a cycle reaching its natural turning point. The situation rests on forces in motion that are larger than any single choice. Understanding where you are in the cycle helps you work with it wisely.
ctx.gift: Your gift is adaptability and a knack for being in the right place at the right time. You can ride change with grace and turn it toward growth. Hidden help comes through timing, luck and the generosity of Jupiter.

name: VIII · Adjustment
title: Adjustment
imagery: A slender, masked woman balances on the very tips of her toes inside a diamond of light, holding a great sword point-down between her feet. From her headdress hang two scales, one bearing Alpha and one Omega, the first and last things weighed against each other. Spheres of light and shadow surround her, showing that every action is met by its exact counterweight.
meaning: Crowley renamed Justice as Adjustment because the universe does not punish or reward; it simply restores balance, the way water finds its level. This card arrives when the scales are moving, when consequences are catching up with causes, and when an honest accounting is needed. It asks you to be precise: to see what is truly yours, what you owe, and what is owed to you, without drama or self-pity. The poised dancer reminds you that balance is not stillness but a living, constant correction. Make the small, clean adjustments now, and the larger picture rights itself.
numerology: Eight is the number of rhythm and regulation, the doubled four that keeps a structure in motion; in the Thoth sequence it marks the point where force is measured and set in order.
affirmation: I make the small, true corrections that bring my life into balance.

ctx.past: A choice, agreement or exchange in the past set the current scales in motion. What is happening now is a fair consequence of what came before, neither cruel nor random. Look back honestly at what was given and what was taken, and you will understand the weight you are carrying.
ctx.present: The heart of the matter is balance. Something is being weighed right now, a contract, a relationship, or your own conscience, and the outcome depends on clear, honest measurement. Stay poised on your toes rather than flat-footed, and keep making the small corrections that keep you upright.
ctx.future: An adjustment is coming: a decision, a settlement, or a natural correction that restores fairness. What has been lopsided will find its level. If you have acted with integrity, the result will feel like relief and like being seen accurately at last.
ctx.challenge: The obstacle is either rigid judgement or a refusal to look at the ledger. You may be keeping score too tightly, demanding perfect fairness from others, or avoiding an accounting you know is due. The dancer cannot balance while gripping; loosen, measure honestly, and act.
ctx.advice: Weigh it carefully, then act cleanly. Gather the facts, separate them from your feelings about them, and make the fair correction, whether that is an apology, a boundary, a payment or a renegotiation. Precision now saves a great deal of turbulence later.
ctx.self: You are in a reflective, discerning mood, trying to see your situation without flattery or blame. You may feel like the one holding the sword of decision. Trust your sense of proportion; you can be both fair and kind to yourself.
ctx.others: People around you may see you as the reasonable one, the person who keeps things fair. Or someone in your environment is a mediator, an official, or a straight-talking friend whose assessment will help tip the scales. Their objectivity is useful, even if it stings.
ctx.hopes: You hope that things will finally even out and that you will be treated fairly. You may also fear judgement, of being found wanting or having to face the consequences of an old choice. Remember that Adjustment restores balance; it does not condemn.
ctx.love: In love, this card asks whether the give and take is truly mutual. A relationship thrives here through honest conversation about needs, chores, money and feelings. If something has tipped too far one way, a calm rebalancing can renew the bond.
ctx.work: At work and with money, attend to contracts, invoices, agreements and the fine print. A fair negotiation, review or settlement is favoured when you come prepared and truthful. Your reputation for reliability is an asset; protect it with careful bookkeeping and clear terms.
ctx.spirit: Spirit reminds you that the universe is a great balancing act and that you are part of it, not its victim. Every action ripples back. Align your Will with what is genuinely true for you, and life begins to cooperate with surprising precision.
ctx.release: Release the need to win or to be right at all costs. Let go of grudges you are keeping as unpaid debts, and of the scorekeeping that leaves no room for grace. Once the account is honestly settled, close the book.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath the surface may be a belief that you deserve less, or that you must always pay more than your share. Alternatively, you may be quietly avoiding responsibility for your own part in the imbalance. Bring either into the light.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a question of fairness: an exchange that was never quite even, or a truth that was weighed and then ignored. Restoring balance there will settle much of what grows above it.
ctx.gift: Your gift is a clear eye and a steady hand. You can see what is out of proportion and gently correct it without drama. That calm discernment makes you trustworthy, and it is exactly what this situation needs.

name: XII · The Hanged Man
title: The Hanged Man
imagery: A pale, blue-green figure hangs head down from an ankh, one leg crossed behind the other, his hands and feet pinned so that he cannot struggle. Behind him lies a grid of green tablets like the floor of the deep sea, a serpent coils around his head and another lies coiled below, waiting. The image is one of total immersion: the old self suspended in the waters until it is ready to be reborn.
meaning: In the Thoth deck the Hanged Man is the card of elemental Water, and his surrender is like drowning into a larger life. He shows the moment when struggling only tightens the bonds, and real change comes from yielding. This is not a punishment but a voluntary pause, a sacrifice of an old way of seeing so that a deeper one can emerge. Crowley considered him a symbol of the old aeon of sacrifice, which invites you to ask which of your sacrifices are wise and which are merely habit. Hang patiently, let the world turn upside down, and notice what becomes visible from this strange angle.
numerology: Twelve gathers the full circle of the zodiac and the months; reduced to three, it is new understanding born from accepting the complete cycle rather than fighting it.
affirmation: I stop struggling and let the deeper current show me the way.

ctx.past: A period of waiting, sacrifice or enforced pause shaped where you are now. Perhaps you gave something up, or life simply held you still for a while. That suspended time taught you more than it seemed to at the moment, and its lessons are still working in you.
ctx.present: You are hanging in the in-between right now, and pushing harder will not cut the rope. The heart of the matter is surrender: letting the situation be what it is while you see it from a completely new angle. The pause itself is doing important work.
ctx.future: A time of stillness is coming, possibly a delay or a turning point where you choose to let go of something. It may feel unproductive, yet it will open a perspective you could never reach by staying busy. Trust the slow tide.
ctx.challenge: The obstacle is martyrdom or stagnation. You may be sacrificing yourself out of habit, waiting for permission, or staying stuck because it feels safer than choosing. Ask whether this suspension still serves you, or whether it has become a place to hide.
ctx.advice: Stop forcing it. Step back, turn the problem upside down, and let your feelings rise to the surface before you decide. Meditation, rest, water and quiet will all help. The answer comes when you relax your grip.
ctx.self: You may feel stuck, out of step with everyone else, or upside down compared with how you used to see things. That disorientation is a sign of real inner change. Be patient with yourself while the new view settles.
ctx.others: Others may not understand your choices right now, and you may look passive or unconventional to them. Alternatively, someone close to you is in a pause or making a sacrifice, and needs patience rather than advice.
ctx.hopes: You hope for release and for a sense that your sacrifices mean something. You may also fear being stuck forever or giving more than you get back. Both feelings point to the same need: to let go willingly, rather than being held against your will.
ctx.love: In love, things may feel suspended: waiting for a decision, a message, or a shift in someone else. Use the pause to look honestly at what you are giving and why. Surrender here means loving without control, not losing yourself.
ctx.work: At work, a project may be on hold or a plan may need to be rethought from the ground up. Do not throw money or effort at a stuck situation. Research, reflect and reframe; the breakthrough idea often comes from looking at it the other way around.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you to dissolve into something larger than your ego's plans. Like water, you can take the shape of what holds you and still remain yourself. A deep, quiet surrender now becomes a source of wisdom later.
ctx.release: Release the need to control the timing. Let go of struggling against what you cannot change, and of old sacrifices that no longer have any purpose. Untie yourself from the role of the one who must always give things up.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a quiet attachment to suffering, as if pain proves worth. Or you may be using waiting as a way to avoid a choice you already know you must make. Look for where you are hanging by your own decision.
ctx.foundation: At the root is a sacrifice or surrender, perhaps a time when you let go of something important, or felt powerless. Understanding what that taught you, rather than what it cost, transforms the whole situation above it.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the ability to see what others miss because you are willing to stop and look differently. Patience, compassion and deep feeling are your strengths now; they let you reach the treasure at the bottom of the sea.

name: XIII · Death
title: Death
imagery: A skeleton crowned like Osiris sweeps a great scythe in a curving dance, and from its blade rise bubbles, each one holding a newly forming life. Around him swirl the creatures of Scorpio: the scorpion, the serpent and the eagle, the three stages of transformation from sting to shedding skin to soaring flight. A lily of the soul and a fish of renewal appear in the depths, showing that every ending feeds a new beginning.
meaning: Death in the Thoth deck is a dance of transformation, not a full stop. Ruled by Scorpio, it speaks of what must decay so that something truer can grow, as autumn leaves become the soil of spring. The scythe clears away worn-out forms, habits and identities, and the bubbles show new life already taking shape. This card rarely signals anything literal; it asks you to let a chapter close with dignity rather than clinging to it. When you stop resisting the change, you will find yourself lighter and remade.
numerology: Thirteen follows the complete twelve, so it breaks the circle open and starts a new cycle; reduced to four, it is the new structure that grows once the old one has been cleared.
affirmation: I let what is finished fall away, and I make room for new life.

ctx.past: A significant ending in your past cleared the ground for who you are today. Something died, a relationship, a role, an identity, and though it hurt, it composted into the strength you now stand on. Honour it as the beginning it secretly was.
ctx.present: You are in the middle of a transformation, and the old form of things is falling away. The heart of the matter is letting go gracefully. What is ending here needs to end, and what is coming cannot arrive until there is space for it.
ctx.future: A chapter is closing and a new one is gestating. Expect a clear ending, followed by a fertile emptiness and then real renewal. It may feel dramatic at first, but in time you will see it as the season that set you free.
ctx.challenge: The challenge is resistance to change, clinging to what is already over because the unknown feels frightening. Or, at the other extreme, you may be cutting things off too harshly. Let the scythe be clean and compassionate rather than fearful or brutal.
ctx.advice: Let it end. Clear out the clutter, finish the thing that is finished, and stop resuscitating what no longer breathes. Grieve if you need to, then turn your attention toward the small new shoots already appearing.
ctx.self: You may feel like you are shedding a skin, no longer who you were and not yet who you are becoming. That in-between state is tender but powerful. Trust that the deep part of you knows how to transform.
ctx.others: Others may sense that you have changed and may react with surprise or unease. Alternatively, someone around you is going through a major ending, and the most useful thing you can offer is steady presence, not fixing.
ctx.hopes: You may hope that a painful situation will finally end, and fear that letting go means losing everything. In truth, Death removes only what has already lived its life. What is essential in you will come through.
ctx.love: In love, Death signals transformation: an old pattern in the relationship needs to end so that a deeper bond can grow, or a connection that has run its course needs to be released. Either way, honesty and grace are the path to renewal.
ctx.work: At work, a role, project or way of earning is coming to its natural end. Restructuring, a career change, or clearing out old commitments makes room for something that fits who you are now. Plan practically, and let the change happen.
ctx.spirit: Spirit reminds you that everything living moves through death and rebirth, the eternal dance of form. Your soul is not your circumstances. When you let the old shapes dissolve, you touch something that does not die.
ctx.release: Release the attachment to how things used to be. Let go of an identity that no longer fits, a resentment you have carried too long, or a hope that has quietly expired. The release itself is the medicine.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a fear of change so deep you do not notice it running your choices. Or there is something you secretly know is over but have not admitted. Naming it takes away much of its power.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies an ending that was never fully grieved or accepted. Until you let that old chapter truly close, it keeps shaping the present. Acknowledge it, and the ground becomes fertile again. The scorpion that stings is also the eagle that will rise.
ctx.gift: Your gift is resilience, the Scorpio power to transform pain into wisdom. You know, deep down, how to begin again. That capacity for rebirth is your greatest protection. Like the snake shedding its skin, you can leave behind what no longer fits and emerge brighter, wiser and more fully yourself.

name: XIV · Art
title: Art
imagery: A two-faced, androgynous figure, one side pale and one dark, stands over a golden cauldron, pouring fire onto water and water onto fire. Below, a white lion and a red eagle have exchanged their colours, and a rainbow arrow rises from the vessel toward the heavens. Around the figure runs a Latin motto urging the seeker to descend into the earth and find the hidden stone, the secret of alchemy.
meaning: Crowley called Temperance Art because it is the great work of combining opposites into something new. Where Lovers shows the marriage, Art shows the alchemy that follows: fire and water, light and dark, masculine and feminine, mixed until they become a third and greater thing. This card asks you to experiment, to blend the seemingly incompatible parts of your life with patience and imagination. It favours creative projects, healing and the slow refinement of your character. Trust the process; real transformation comes from combining things carefully, one measure at a time.
numerology: Fourteen is twice seven, the doubling of the mystical number; reduced to five, it is change and motion harnessed into a deliberate, creative process.
affirmation: I blend every part of myself into something new and beautiful.

ctx.past: In the past you learned to combine things that did not seem to belong together, perhaps two cultures, two careers, or two sides of your own nature. That early alchemy is part of your foundation now. It taught you that opposites can feed each other.
ctx.present: You are in the middle of a creative fusion. The heart of the matter is integration: bringing together different elements, people or ideas into a working whole. Keep stirring the cauldron patiently; the mixture is not finished yet, but it is becoming gold.
ctx.future: A creative breakthrough or a healing synthesis is on its way. Things that felt at odds will start to work together, and you will find a third way through. Expect projects, partnerships or inner work to come together with surprising harmony.
ctx.challenge: The challenge is imbalance in the mixture: too much fire or too much water, impatience or excess caution. You may be trying to keep the opposites apart, or rushing the process. Alchemy takes time and careful measure; respect the timing.
ctx.advice: Experiment. Combine your talents, try the unlikely partnership, mix the practical with the visionary. Take it a step at a time, adjusting as you go. Your aim is not compromise but a creative new whole.
ctx.self: You may feel like several people at once, with contradictory desires and talents. Art says that is your raw material, not your problem. Embrace your complexity, and you become your own masterpiece. The two faces of the Art figure are both you, and both belong.
ctx.others: Others may see you as a bridge-builder, someone who can bring different people or ideas together. Or someone in your environment acts as a catalyst, mixing things up in ways that will ultimately create something valuable.
ctx.hopes: You hope to bring the scattered parts of your life together into a meaningful whole. You may fear that some pieces will never fit. Art promises they can, if you are willing to experiment and refine.
ctx.love: In love, Art speaks of two different people creating something that neither could make alone. Differences are not obstacles but ingredients. Patience, playfulness and mutual respect will turn the mix into a lasting and creative bond.
ctx.work: At work, combine skills or disciplines in an original way. Creative industries, healing professions and research are especially favoured. A careful, iterative approach to money and projects works better than big, sudden moves. Small tests and adjustments will show you the right formula.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you into the great work of self-transformation. You are the cauldron, the fire and the water all at once. Every experience, light or dark, can be refined into wisdom when you hold it with patience.
ctx.release: Release either-or thinking. Let go of the belief that you must choose one side of yourself and abandon the other. Drop perfectionism too; alchemy is messy before it is golden. Let the mixture bubble and change colour before it settles.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a part of yourself you have rejected as incompatible with who you are supposed to be. Until it is invited into the mixture, the work will feel incomplete. The lion needs the eagle.
ctx.foundation: At the root is a need to reconcile opposites, two values, two loyalties, or two inner voices pulling in different directions. Finding the synthesis between them is the key to everything built above. The fire and the water both have something essential to give.
ctx.gift: Your gift is creative alchemy: the ability to combine, refine and transform. You can turn conflict into collaboration and raw experience into art. That talent is rare, and it is exactly what this moment calls for.

name: XV · The Devil
title: The Devil
imagery: A goat with great spiralling horns and a third eye grins out from the card, standing before a towering tree-like stalk whose roots hold figures straining to break free. A winged staff topped with the sun rests beside him, and the mountains of Capricorn rise behind. The goat is Pan, the wild, laughing creative force of nature, delighting in all things, high and low alike.
meaning: The Thoth Devil is less a tempter than the raw, creative power of matter itself: Pan, the joyous and fertile energy that pushes life upward through rock and soil. Ruled by Capricorn, he is ambition, endurance and the pleasure of the senses. This card asks you to own your desires and your drive, rather than being secretly ruled by them. Where you feel bound, notice that the chains are often self-made and can be loosened with honesty and humour. Used consciously, this energy builds, creates and enjoys life to the full.
numerology: Fifteen reduces to six, harmony and desire, but its root of five plus ten adds restless matter and appetite; it is the drive to make the material world beautiful and to enjoy it.
affirmation: I own my desires and use my power to create.

ctx.past: In the past, strong desires, ambitions or attachments shaped your path. Perhaps a habit, a relationship or a goal had a powerful hold on you. That intensity taught you about your own appetite and endurance, and it fuels your capability now.
ctx.present: Raw, earthy energy is at the heart of the matter. Desire, ambition, money or physical pleasure are central right now. The question is whether you are using this power consciously, or whether it is quietly using you.
ctx.future: A period of strong drive and material focus is coming. Expect ambition, sensuality or a tempting opportunity. It can bring real achievement if you stay awake to your motives and keep a sense of humour about your own appetites.
ctx.challenge: The challenge is compulsion: habits, attachments or fears that feel like chains. You may be stuck in a pattern of overwork, overindulgence or control. Look closely at the binding; it is often looser than you think, and the first step is admitting it is there.
ctx.advice: Acknowledge what you really want, without shame. Then put that energy to work on something worth building. Climb steadily like the mountain goat, laugh at your own excesses, and choose your attachments rather than being chosen by them.
