ctx.gift: Your gift is gentle imagination and intuitive sensitivity. You bring beauty, kindness and dreamlike magic into the world, and you can help dreams take tangible form. Like the swan that crowns her head, you move through life with a grace that softens and uplifts everyone around you.

name: Knight of Cups
title: Fire of Water
imagery: A winged warrior in armour rides a white horse leaping over the sea, holding a cup from which a crab emerges, with a peacock rising behind him. The waters beneath are calm and clear. The crab is the sign of Cancer, the peacock a symbol of beauty and the many colours of the soul, and the leaping horse shows feeling turned into swift, graceful action.
meaning: The Knight of Cups is Fire of Water: the swift, active, passionate part of feeling. He rides toward his ideal with grace and enthusiasm, carrying love and inspiration into the world. Crowley described him as graceful, amiable and sensitive, sometimes passive or too easily swayed, yet full of feeling. In a reading he can be a romantic, idealistic person or the arrival of an offer, an invitation or a new emotional adventure. He asks you to follow your heart with courage while keeping your feet on the stirrups.
numerology: The Knight is the Yod of the divine name, the swift and fiery first rush of the suit; in Water it is feeling that charges into motion.
affirmation: I follow my heart with courage and grace.

ctx.past: A romantic or idealistic impulse set this situation in motion, an offer, an invitation or a passionate decision made with the heart. Its charm and enthusiasm still echo in how things stand now. Like his leaping white horse, that first rush of feeling carried you further than caution would have.
ctx.present: Feeling is in motion. You are pursuing an ideal, a person or a dream with energy and enthusiasm. The heart of the matter is whether that passion is rooted in reality or racing ahead of it.
ctx.future: An invitation, offer or romantic adventure is coming toward you, perhaps carried by a charming person. Let yourself be swept up a little, but keep your eyes open to what is truly being offered. As Fire of Water, it will arrive quickly and warmly.
ctx.challenge: The Knight’s shadow is being moved by every passing feeling, or chasing an ideal that cannot be reached. Charm without follow-through can disappoint. Let passion carry commitment, not replace it; as Fire of Water, he must keep the flame from boiling the sea.
ctx.advice: Follow your heart. Make the gesture, send the message, pursue the creative dream. Bring grace and sincerity to your actions, and let your feelings guide you while your judgement steers; like his leaping white horse, move swiftly but with poise.
ctx.self: You are in a passionate, idealistic mood, ready to act on what you feel. Your enthusiasm is inspiring. Remember to pause and check that your heart and head are riding the same horse; as Fire of Water, you carry warmth into everything you touch.
ctx.others: Others see you as charming, romantic and inspiring. Someone around you may be courting you, making an offer or bringing new energy and idealism into your life. The peacock behind him suggests someone colourful, artistic and eager to be admired, so enjoy their spark while gently testing their sincerity.
ctx.hopes: You hope for a romantic or inspiring adventure that sweeps you away. You may fear that ideals never survive contact with reality. The Knight says they can, if you ride with grace; the calm waters beneath his leap show that passion can be steady.
ctx.love: Romance is on the move. An admirer may appear, or a relationship gains new passion and gestures of affection. Enjoy the courtship, and look for sincerity behind the charm; like the crab emerging from his cup, true tenderness may hide beneath the armour.
ctx.work: An exciting offer or creative opportunity may arrive. Your enthusiasm opens doors. Bring your ideas forward with confidence, and follow through with practical steps; as Fire of Water, he brings feeling and imagination into action, so pitch the idea that moves you and let your sincerity sell it.
ctx.spirit: Your guides invite you on a quest of the heart. Spiritual passion and devotion are strong now. Let your idealism carry you toward real experience, not just beautiful visions; the peacock’s many colours show the soul’s full spectrum unfolding as you ride.
ctx.release: Release the habit of chasing whatever feels exciting in the moment. Let go of unrealistic ideals that keep you from appreciating what is real and present. The calm sea beneath his leaping horse shows that real passion does not need constant novelty, so let a steady commitment be enough.
ctx.shadow: Hidden here may be a tendency to fall in love with the idea of something rather than the thing itself, or to avoid deeper commitment by staying always on the move. The crab in his cup hints at a tender heart he guards behind charm.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies an emotional impulse, a passionate idea or desire that set things moving. Understanding what truly motivated it reveals much. The crab rising from his cup suggests that beneath the dash lies a longing for home and belonging, and that longing drives the whole story.
ctx.gift: Your gift is inspired passion. You can carry love, beauty and enthusiasm into the world and spark the hearts of others. Your grace in action is magnetic; like the winged rider leaping over the sea, you carry hope and beauty to places that need them, and you make the journey look effortless.

name: Queen of Cups
title: Water of Water
imagery: A veiled queen sits enthroned on still water, her form almost dissolved into shimmering reflections and curving lines of light. She holds a shell-shaped cup from which a crayfish emerges, with a lotus in her other hand and an ibis standing beside her. The reflections show her mirror-like receptivity, the ibis is the bird of Thoth and wisdom, and the lotus is the open, receptive soul.
meaning: The Queen of Cups is Water of Water, the purest form of feeling: reflective, receptive and deep. She mirrors whatever comes to her, so that others see themselves in her. Crowley described her as dreamy, tranquil and poetic, the perfect reflection of whatever looks into her. In a reading she can be a deeply intuitive, empathic person or the call to trust your inner knowing and emotional depths. She asks you to be still, to listen beneath the surface and to honour the wisdom of feeling.
numerology: The Queen is the first He of the divine name, the receptive mother who receives and reflects; in Water she is feeling in its most pure and mirror-like form.
affirmation: I trust the deep, still wisdom of my feelings.

ctx.past: Behind this situation lies a time of deep feeling, intuition or quiet reflection. Perhaps a nurturing person shaped you, or you learned to listen inwardly. That wisdom remains a still pool you can return to.
ctx.present: Intuition and emotion are your guides right now. The heart of the matter lies beneath the surface, in what you feel and sense rather than what you can prove. Be still and listen inwardly; like the Queen on her still throne, let the surface settle so you can see clearly.
ctx.future: A period of deep insight and emotional clarity is coming, or an intuitive, compassionate person will enter your life. Expect your inner knowing to become stronger and more trustworthy. The still waters around her throne promise a calmer, clearer inner life.
ctx.challenge: The Queen’s shadow is losing yourself in others’ feelings, reflecting everyone so well that your own shape disappears. Boundaries matter. Your empathy is a gift only when you remember who you are; her veil can hide as much as it protects.
ctx.advice: Turn inward. Meditate, journal, sit near water, and listen to what your feelings and dreams are telling you. Offer compassion, but keep a quiet centre that belongs to you alone; let the stillness of her waters become your practice.
ctx.self: You are deeply sensitive and intuitive right now, attuned to subtle currents in yourself and others. Honour that sensitivity; it gives you wisdom that logic alone cannot reach. Like the Queen veiled in shimmering light, your depth is real even when others cannot fully see it.
ctx.others: Others see you as empathic, understanding and mysterious, and they may come to you to be heard. Someone near you may be a deeply intuitive or nurturing presence. Because she reflects whoever looks at her, people may see their own feelings in you more than they see you.
ctx.hopes: You hope to be truly understood and to live in tune with your inner truth. You may fear being overwhelmed by feeling. The Queen shows that still water can hold great depths safely; her cup, with its crayfish rising from the depths, shows feeling can be held safely.
ctx.love: Love is deep, tender and intuitive. Emotional understanding is strong between partners. Make sure both of you are being seen, not just reflected, and that your own needs are spoken; like her mirror-still waters, love here reflects each partner back with great tenderness.
ctx.work: Intuition guides your work well now. Caring, creative or counselling roles are favoured. Trust your instincts in decisions, and bring compassion to colleagues and clients; the ibis beside her is the bird of Thoth, god of wisdom and writing, so careful listening, research and patient reflection serve you especially well.
ctx.spirit: Your guides speak in reflections, dreams and quiet feelings. The ibis of Thoth brings wisdom through stillness. Your intuitive and psychic gifts are particularly open now; her lotus is the open soul, ready to receive whatever the deep waters bring up, so keep a dream journal by your bed.
ctx.release: Release the habit of absorbing others’ emotions as your own. Let go of moods that are not truly yours, and return to the clear stillness of your own waters. As Water of Water, you are meant to reflect, not absorb.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath may be a fear of your own depths, or a tendency to show others only what they want to see. Look at what you keep veiled, even from yourself. As Water of Water, her depths are endless, but she need not fear them.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this matter lies deep emotion and intuition. What is happening grows from feelings and inner knowings that may not yet have been put into words. The crayfish rising from her cup hints at instincts slowly surfacing.
ctx.gift: Your gift is profound empathy and intuitive wisdom. You can understand others deeply and reflect back truths they need to see. Your stillness is a sanctuary; like the ibis of Thoth beside her throne, you hold a quiet wisdom that others trust, and they leave your company feeling clearer and calmer.

name: Prince of Cups
title: Air of Water
imagery: A young prince rides in a chariot drawn by an eagle across stormy waters beneath falling rain. He holds a lotus in one hand and a cup with a serpent rising from it in the other, and an eagle crowns his helmet. The eagle and serpent are both symbols of Scorpio, showing transformation, the lotus shows the soul, and the falling rain is feeling pouring down into the world.
meaning: The Prince of Cups is Air of Water: the intellect and imagination of feeling, often volatile and intensely creative. Crowley described him as subtle and secretive, an artist on the surface whose calm can hide great depths of passion. In a reading he can be an emotionally complex, magnetic person or your own powerful feelings seeking expression. He asks you to channel intense emotion into creation and understanding rather than secrecy or manipulation. Your depth is a source of art, insight and transformation.
numerology: The Prince is the Vau of the divine name, the son who carries the union of Knight and Queen into the world; in Water he gives feeling direction, form and voice.
affirmation: I channel my deep feelings into creation and understanding.

ctx.past: A powerful emotional current lies behind this situation, perhaps a secret passion, an intense relationship or a creative surge. It may have stayed hidden, yet it still shapes what is happening now. The eagle and serpent of Scorpio hint that it was quietly transforming you all along.
ctx.present: Deep feelings are stirring, possibly ones you have not shown to anyone. The heart of the matter is finding a healthy channel for them. Expressed creatively, they become power; hidden, they become pressure; like the serpent rising from his cup, what is hidden wants to emerge.
ctx.future: Intense emotion or a magnetic, complex person will come into play. Expect depth, creativity and some mystery. Transformation is possible if you meet it with honesty rather than control; like the rain falling around his chariot, feelings will pour freely.
ctx.challenge: The Prince’s shadow is secrecy, emotional manipulation or calm that hides a storm. Unspoken feelings can make you unpredictable. Bring them into the open with care, and let them transform you; as Air of Water, he can think his way around feeling.
ctx.advice: Give your feelings a voice and a form. Write, paint, make music or have the honest conversation. Use your insight into others’ hearts to understand and connect, never to control; like the eagle drawing his chariot, rise above the storm to see clearly.
ctx.self: You are emotionally intense and perceptive at the moment, perhaps more than you show. Your inner world is rich and powerful. Trust it, and find ways to share it; as Air of Water, you can name feelings others cannot, and turn them into words, images or music that carry real weight.
ctx.others: Others may see you as calm, mysterious or hard to read. Someone in your environment may be magnetic and creative but emotionally guarded. Patience and honesty open the way; like the eagle crest on his helm, they watch closely before they reveal themselves.
ctx.hopes: You hope to express your deepest self and be truly met in your intensity. You may fear exposing feelings that seem too strong. The Prince shows that depth, shared wisely, is a gift; like the serpent rising from his cup, your intensity can heal and renew.
ctx.love: Love is passionate, intense and perhaps secretive. A magnetic attraction may be at work. Build trust by being open about what you feel, and let the relationship transform you both; the rain around his chariot shows feelings that need to fall freely.
ctx.work: Creative and strategic work thrives. Artistic or psychological insight gives you an edge. Keep motives transparent, and channel your intensity into real achievement; as Air of Water, you bring emotional intelligence into strategy and art alike, so trust your reading of people and let your work carry real feeling.
ctx.spirit: Your guides invite you into transformation. The eagle and serpent show the soul rising from the depths. Use your emotional power for healing and spiritual growth; Scorpio’s serpent sheds its skin to grow, and you are invited to do the same, letting an old self fall away so a truer one can rise.
ctx.release: Release the need to hide or control your feelings. Let go of secrets that no longer protect you and patterns of emotional strategy that keep real intimacy away. The eagle drawing his chariot can lift you above old patterns.
ctx.shadow: Hidden beneath may be a fear of your own power or of being truly known. Notice where you hold feelings back as a form of protection or control. The serpent coiled in his cup holds the energy you guard most closely.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this matter lie strong, perhaps unspoken feelings. Much of what is happening grows from emotional currents that run deep beneath a calm surface. As Air of Water, the Prince turns feeling into thought and plan, so look closely at the motives behind the calm, composed surface.
ctx.gift: Your gift is emotional depth turned into creative and transformative power. You can understand the hidden heart of things and express it in ways that move and heal others. Like the lotus he carries alongside the serpent, you hold both tenderness and power in balance.

name: Ace of Swords
title: Root of the Powers of Air
imagery: A great upright sword rises through parting clouds, its blade inscribed with the Greek word Thelema, meaning Will, and its point thrust through a radiant crown of twenty-two rays. Light breaks open the grey sky around it. The crown speaks of the mind serving something higher, and the twenty-two rays echo the paths of the Tree of Life: intellect at its finest, wielded by true Will.
meaning: The Ace of Swords is the seed of Air itself, the pure power of mind before it splits into argument and doubt. In the Thoth tradition it is the sword of the magician’s Will, cutting through confusion so that a single clear truth stands up in the light. When it appears, a breakthrough in understanding is near: a realisation, a decision, a word that finally names what was hidden. This is thinking that serves your deeper purpose rather than your anxieties. Use it cleanly, because a blade this bright can liberate or wound depending on the hand that holds it.
astrology: Root of Air · Kether of Swords; rules the quadrant of the heavens from Capricorn through Pisces
numerology: The Ace is Kether, the One: undivided potential and the first spark of the suit before any number shapes it.
affirmation: My mind is a clear blade in the service of my true Will.

ctx.past: A moment of sudden clarity shaped what came before. Perhaps a truth was spoken aloud, or you finally saw a situation for what it was. That cut was clean, and the decision it set in motion still runs underneath everything that is happening now.
ctx.present: A sharp new understanding is breaking through the clouds right now. You can see what you could not see before, and the heart of the matter is what you will do with that clarity. Name the truth plainly; it is the beginning of real change.
ctx.future: A breakthrough is coming: an idea, a conversation, or a decision that clears the air. Expect the fog to lift quite suddenly. What follows will ask you to act on what you now know, so let your Will, not your fear, take hold of the hilt.
ctx.challenge: The danger of the Ace is a mind that cuts everything, including what deserves tenderness. Brilliant certainty can harden into coldness, or you may be thinking so much that you forget to act. Ask whether your clarity serves your purpose or just your need to be right.
ctx.advice: Say the true thing, simply and without decoration. Write the idea down, make the decision, draw the line you have been circling for weeks. One honest cut now will save you a hundred small wounds of hesitation later.
ctx.self: You are in a lucid, decisive frame of mind, or you are ready to be. Trust your intelligence. You know more than you have been admitting, and your ability to see straight through to the point is one of your most valuable tools right now.
ctx.others: Others may see you as sharp, articulate and refreshingly direct. Alternatively, someone around you is bringing a truth into the open that changes the conversation. Their honesty may sting for a moment, but it clears the way for something better.
ctx.hopes: You hope for clarity and fear the cost of it: seeing something you cannot unsee, or saying something you cannot take back. Both are signs that the truth is already close. Clarity tends to feel lighter once you stop resisting it.
ctx.love: In love, this is a card of honest conversation. Something needs naming, whether it is a need, a boundary or a feeling. A fresh, clear-eyed start is possible when both people are willing to say what is real rather than what is comfortable.
ctx.work: A brilliant idea, a strategic decision or a winning proposal is at hand. This favours writing, analysis, problem-solving and any work that rewards precision. Cut away what is unnecessary and let the core concept stand on its own.
ctx.spirit: The divine message is that your mind can be a sacred instrument. Crowley’s sword bears the word Will: thought aligned with your deepest purpose. Meditation, study or a single honest intention can open a channel of remarkable insight right now.
ctx.release: Release muddled thinking and the habit of keeping every option open forever. Let go of the stories that blur what you already know. Clarity requires choosing, and choosing means letting some possibilities fall away for good.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the surface you may be using cleverness as armour, keeping feelings at a safe intellectual distance. Or you already know the answer and are pretending to still be undecided. The hidden blade is the truth you have not yet let yourself wield.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies a single idea, belief or decision. Find it and the rest makes sense. Everything else grew from that seed of thought, which means changing your mind at the root can change the whole tree.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the capacity to see clearly and speak plainly. In a world full of noise, that is rare and powerful. When you combine your sharp mind with a sincere purpose, you can cut through almost any knot.

name: Two of Swords
title: Peace
imagery: Two crossed swords meet at their points through a five-petalled blue rose, the flower of harmony binding them together. Behind them spins a soft, geometric pattern like a turning pinwheel, and small daggers bear the signs of the Moon and Libra. The rose shows love reconciling opposing thoughts, while the steady pattern shows a mind that has found its balance point.
meaning: Peace is the first moment the restless mind finds equilibrium. With the Moon in Libra, it brings a gentle, receptive calm, where two opposing ideas stop fighting and rest together. This is not avoidance but genuine reconciliation: the quarrel has paused and something softer holds the tension. Use this calm to listen, to weigh things fairly and to let your thoughts settle like silt in clear water. The Moon is changeable, so treasure this peace and tend it; it is a living balance, not a permanent state.
numerology: Two is Chokmah, the first movement of force; in the restless suit of Air it appears as balance, the two blades held still by a single rose.
affirmation: I hold opposing truths in peace and let my mind grow still.

ctx.past: A season of calm or a reconciliation lies behind you. Perhaps a conflict was settled, or you found a way to live with two competing truths. That balance taught you something about fairness and patience that is still useful now.
ctx.present: Right now the swords are resting crossed through the rose. A quarrel has cooled, a decision is on pause, or your mind has found an unusual stillness. Enjoy the peace, and notice what becomes clearer when you stop pushing.
ctx.future: Calm is coming. A tension will ease, an argument will soften or two sides will find a middle ground they can both stand on. The Moon in Libra suggests this peace arrives gently, through listening and compromise rather than victory.
ctx.challenge: Peace can slide into stalemate if you use it to avoid what needs deciding. Are you keeping things balanced because it is right, or because choosing feels frightening? A truce is a breathing space, not a hiding place.
ctx.advice: Seek the middle way. Listen to both sides, including both voices inside you, before you act. Breathe, soften your jaw and let the rose of goodwill sit between the swords. A calm mind will choose better than a hurried one.
ctx.self: You are in a diplomatic, even-handed mood, able to see both sides of the story. That fairness is a real strength. Just make sure you include your own needs in the balance and do not simply keep the peace for everyone else.
ctx.others: Others see you as a peacemaker, someone calm and reasonable in a tense situation. Or your environment itself is entering a quieter phase, where people are willing to talk rather than fight. Your steadiness helps that peace take root.
ctx.hopes: You hope for harmony and may fear that any peace will be fragile. Both feelings are natural under a changeable Moon. Peace grows stronger every time it is chosen again, so you have more power over its lasting than you think.
ctx.love: In love, this card brings reconciliation and a softening of old arguments. Two people can meet in the middle with kindness. It favours honest, gentle talks and the decision to value the bond more than being right.
ctx.work: At work, negotiations go well and disputes can be settled fairly. It is a good time for mediation, partnership agreements and calm planning. Do not rush to force an outcome; patient, balanced judgement will pay off and earn you lasting respect.
ctx.spirit: Spirit invites you to find the still point between opposites. Meditation, breath work or simply sitting quietly can show you that the mind, left to settle, is naturally peaceful. The rose at the centre is love holding all things together.
ctx.release: Release the need to win every argument, especially the ones inside your head. Let go of the urge to resolve everything immediately. Some tensions ease on their own once you stop feeding them with worry.
ctx.shadow: Hidden under this calm may be an unmade choice. Peace can disguise indecision or quiet resentment. Look gently at whether something unspoken is waiting beneath the surface of this calm, asking to be heard with kindness.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a desire for fairness and harmony. This situation grew from an attempt to balance competing needs, yours and other people’s. Understanding that original wish for peace helps you honour it now.
ctx.gift: Your gift is diplomacy: the ability to hold contradictions without being torn apart by them. You can calm a room, bridge two sides and let love be the rose that binds opposing ideas together into something whole.

name: Three of Swords
title: Sorrow
imagery: A great upright sword pierces the heart of a rose while two curved swords cut into it from either side, so that its petals fall away. Behind them a heavy, stormy sky presses down in dark greys and violets. The falling petals show beauty lost, and the storm shows the weight of sorrow, yet the central sword stands straight: understanding born through pain.
meaning: Sorrow is Saturn in Libra: the heavy planet of time and limitation entering the sign of relationships and balance. It describes grief, disappointment and the ache of a painful truth, but in the Thoth tradition it is also the dark womb in which deeper understanding is formed. Three is the number of Binah, the Great Mother, who gives form through restriction and sorrow. This card does not ask you to pretend you are fine. It asks you to feel what is here, honestly and fully, because sorrow that is allowed to move becomes wisdom, and sorrow that is resisted turns into bitterness.
numerology: Three is Binah, the Great Mother and the first form of understanding; in Air she brings comprehension through grief.
affirmation: I let my sorrow move through me, and it leaves wisdom behind.

ctx.past: A loss, betrayal or disappointment lies in your recent history. It may still ache, and that is natural. The understanding you gained through that sorrow is now part of who you are, even if the lesson came at a high price.
ctx.present: Something hurts right now, and the card honours that. A painful truth has come to light or a hope has fallen away. The heart of the matter is to let yourself grieve rather than intellectualise the pain into silence.
ctx.future: A season of sadness or a hard truth may be approaching. It is not a punishment, and it does not last forever. Allowing yourself to feel it will lead through to a clearer, wiser place on the other side of the storm.
ctx.challenge: The challenge is getting stuck in sorrow: replaying the wound, feeding melancholy with old thoughts or wearing grief as an identity. Saturn asks for patience, not wallowing. Let the rain fall, then let it pass.
ctx.advice: Allow yourself to feel. Cry if you need to, write it down, talk to someone you trust. Treat your heart as you would a dear friend’s. Honest grief is a kind of cleansing, and you do not need to rush it.
ctx.self: You may be feeling wounded, sombre or disillusioned. Be gentle with yourself. This does not make you weak; it means you cared deeply. Your sensitivity is also the source of your compassion, and it will return as strength.
ctx.others: Someone around you may be carrying grief, or the atmosphere itself is heavy with disappointment. Others might see you as sad or withdrawn right now. Kindness and honesty go a long way in this climate.
ctx.hopes: You may fear being hurt again, and that fear can shape your choices. Your hope is that the pain will mean something. It can: sorrow that is felt and processed well becomes understanding, tenderness and resilience.
ctx.love: In love, there may be heartache, a painful truth or a sense of distance. This card asks for honest acknowledgement rather than blame. Healing begins when the hurt is spoken aloud and heard with patience and care.
ctx.work: At work there may be disappointment, a setback or a cutting remark. Take it seriously but do not let it define you. What you learn from this experience will make your future work wiser and more grounded.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through sorrow as the Great Mother who teaches by limitation. Even the darkest storm passes. Let grief open your heart rather than close it, and it will deepen your understanding of yourself and others.
ctx.release: Release old sorrows you have been carrying long past their season. Let go of the thoughts that keep reopening the wound. You can honour what was lost without holding on to the pain forever; love remains when the ache softens.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be a grief you have not admitted, perhaps buried under busyness or cheerfulness. Unfelt sadness tends to leak out sideways as irritability, numbness or tiredness. Gently look beneath the surface and let it be felt.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies a wound or loss that has never fully healed. Recognising it with compassion is the first step. Much of what is happening now grows from that old heartache.
ctx.gift: Your gift is emotional depth and the ability to understand others’ pain because you have known your own. Through sorrow you have gained a quiet, hard-won wisdom that can comfort and guide those around you.

name: Four of Swords
title: Truce
imagery: Four swords meet point to point at the heart of a great rose of forty-nine petals, set in the shape of a cross against a calm, ordered field of blue and grey. The swords are sheathed in the rose rather than fighting, and the strict symmetry shows a mind that has drawn up terms. It is the picture of a ceasefire: conflict held still by agreement and order.
meaning: Truce is Jupiter in Libra: the generous, ordering planet in the sign of balance and fair dealing. After the sorrow of the Three, the mind withdraws to recover and to make terms, with others or with itself. This is rest, convalescence of the spirit, a negotiated calm in which you can breathe again. Crowley noted that a truce can also be a convention that simply postpones real resolution, so use the pause consciously. Rest deeply, restore your strength, and let the quiet show you what genuinely needs settling before you take up the sword again.
numerology: Four is Chesed, the sphere of Jupiter, law and stable order; in restless Air it imposes a truce that halts the struggle for a while.
affirmation: I accept the pause I am given and let my mind heal in peace.

ctx.past: Behind you lies a time when you had to step back from a struggle and lay down your arms. That retreat was wiser than it may have felt. The rest and reflection you gained then gave you a steadier footing, and the terms you agreed to are still shaping things now.
ctx.present: A ceasefire is in place, around you or inside your own head. The fighting has stopped for now, and you have a precious breathing space. The heart of the matter is using it well: resting, recovering and reflecting instead of rushing straight back into the fray.
ctx.future: A lull is coming. Expect a tense situation to quieten, an agreement to be reached or a welcome stretch of rest after effort. Jupiter’s blessing on this pause means it can genuinely restore you, so plan to slow down rather than fill the space with new battles.
ctx.challenge: A truce can harden into a comfortable avoidance. If you keep the peace by never mentioning the real problem, the swords stay in the rose but the conflict waits underneath. This card asks you to rest, yes, but also to be honest about what this calm is postponing.
ctx.advice: Withdraw for a while. Clear your calendar where you can, sleep, walk, sit quietly and let your nervous system settle. If there is a dispute, offer fair terms and a cooling-off period. A rested mind will see solutions that an exhausted one keeps missing.
ctx.self: You may feel tired, quiet or in need of solitude, and that is exactly right for now. Taking time out is not giving up. You are gathering yourself, and your instinct to step back from the noise is one you can trust.
ctx.others: People around you may notice you are more withdrawn than usual, and most will respect it. Or the wider environment is entering a calmer, more diplomatic phase, where former opponents are prepared to talk. Take advantage of the goodwill while it lasts.
ctx.hopes: You may long for peace and fear it is only temporary. Both are honest feelings. A truce becomes lasting peace when it is used to address the underlying issue gently, so this fragile calm is also a real opportunity you can build on.
ctx.love: In love, a quieter, more reflective phase allows wounds to close. Some space, or simply a pause in a recurring argument, can do wonders. When you come back together, do it with fair terms and calmer hearts, and the bond can be stronger for the rest.
ctx.work: At work, step back to plan, reorganise or renegotiate. This favours contracts, mediation and sensible schedules over heroic pushes. If you have been running on fumes, build real rest into your routine; your best work will come after the pause, not during the burnout.
ctx.spirit: Spirit is inviting you into retreat and contemplation. The many-petalled rose at the centre suggests that the deepest peace is found within, in stillness rather than effort. A quiet day, a period of prayer or meditation, can let your guides be heard.
ctx.release: Release the belief that you must be constantly busy, alert or fighting to be worthwhile. Let go of the inner chatter that keeps reopening old quarrels. You are allowed to put the swords down and rest without first earning it.
ctx.shadow: Beneath this calm there may be an agreement that suits nobody, kept only to avoid discomfort. Ask gently whether the peace you are keeping is real or merely polite. What you refuse to discuss tends to wait patiently for the truce to end.
ctx.foundation: At the root of the situation is depletion: a mind and heart that needed to stop. Much of what is happening grows from that need for order and recovery after strain. Honour it, and the rest of the picture begins to make sense.
ctx.gift: Your gift is knowing when to stop. You can bring order to turbulence, broker fair terms and create a calm space where others can breathe. That steady, peacemaking quality is a real strength, and it will serve you well right now.

name: Five of Swords
title: Defeat
imagery: Five swords with bent, notched and broken blades form an inverted pentagram, each hilt different from the others, while the torn petals of a rose drift between them. The background is unsettled and fractured. The broken blades show thought that has lost its edge, the scattered petals the harmony of the Four undone, and the inverted star a moment when circumstance overrules spirit.
meaning: Defeat is Venus in Aquarius. Gentle, peace-loving Venus is out of her depth in this cool, detached sign, and the result is a mind that loses heart before the contest is truly decided. Crowley saw it as defeat through weakness, through softness at the wrong moment or through simply expecting to lose. It is a setback rather than a final judgement. Look honestly at where your thinking gave up too soon, where you surrendered to avoid conflict or talked yourself into failure. Recovering your nerve is the real work this card sets you, and it is entirely within your reach.
numerology: Five is Geburah, the sphere of Mars, severity and upheaval; in Air it breaks the calm of the Four and tests the strength of the mind.
affirmation: Even when I lose a round, I keep my nerve and rise wiser.

ctx.past: A loss, a failed plan or a moment of humiliation sits in your recent past. Perhaps you gave way too easily, or never quite believed you could win. That experience still stings, but it also showed you precisely where your confidence needs rebuilding.
ctx.present: Something has not gone your way, and your mind may now be filling in the worst possible story about it. You feel deflated or outmanoeuvred. The heart of the matter is whether this setback becomes a lesson you use or a verdict you accept about yourself.
ctx.future: A plan may falter or an argument may be lost ahead. This is not the end of the road. Treat it as information: what was weak in the strategy, where did your nerve waver? Adjust, regroup and you can approach the next round much better armed.
ctx.challenge: The real enemy here is defeatism. Your own thoughts may be undermining you, rehearsing failure until it feels inevitable. There may also be a tendency to give in to keep the peace. Notice when you surrender before anyone has even asked you to.
ctx.advice: Acknowledge the loss honestly, then stop replaying it. Choose carefully which battles are worth fighting, and where you do engage, commit fully instead of half-heartedly. One small act of courage today will start to repair the confidence this card has bruised.
ctx.self: You may feel beaten, small or unsure of your worth. Be truthful about the hurt, but do not turn it into self-punishment. A setback says something about a situation, not about the whole of who you are, and your strength will return faster with kindness.
ctx.others: Others may read you as discouraged or unusually passive. Or the mood around you is one of low morale, with people expecting the worst. You can refuse to absorb that atmosphere, and perhaps even become the person who restores a little hope.
ctx.hopes: The fear here is of failing, or of being shown up, and fear like that can quietly arrange its own fulfilment. Underneath lies a hope of regaining your dignity. That begins not with a grand victory but with deciding to try again.
ctx.love: In love, someone may feel they keep losing, or one of you gives in too readily to avoid friction. That leaves resentment behind. Look for conversations where neither person has to be defeated for the other to feel heard, and speak your needs plainly.
ctx.work: At work, a proposal may be turned down or a project may stall. Review what happened with clear eyes, without blame or catastrophising. Better preparation and steadier nerve can turn this round, and the lesson you take now is worth keeping.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks gently through defeat. When the ego is bruised, there is room for humility and for a deeper part of you to be heard. Losing gracefully can be a strange initiation, clearing away pride so that a truer strength can grow.
ctx.release: Let go of the internal commentary that predicts failure and replays every misstep. Release, too, the need to win every quarrel. Both drain your energy. Keep the lesson, drop the self-reproach, and you will have far more to bring to the next effort.
ctx.shadow: Hidden under this defeat may be a fear of conflict dressed up as niceness. If you habitually avoid confrontation, you may then feel overrun by the results. Gentle people can still be firm; kindness and a backbone work well together.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a crack in your confidence, perhaps from an old loss you never fully recovered from. That memory still whispers that you will not succeed. Recognising its voice for what it is weakens its hold.
ctx.gift: Your gift is resilience earned the hard way. You know what losing feels like, which gives you humility and empathy for others who struggle. That knowledge, joined with renewed courage, makes you formidable the next time you step forward.

name: Six of Swords
title: Science
imagery: Six swords point inward from the edges to touch a rose cross at the centre, framed by a radiant hexagram in harmonious, luminous colours. The design is ordered and perfectly balanced. Each blade is a line of reasoning, and their meeting on the rose cross shows many thoughts converging on one truth, intellect married to the heart and to spiritual insight.
meaning: Science is Mercury in Aquarius: the planet of the mind at home in the sign of objective, original thought. After the defeat of the Five, intelligence regains its balance through method, observation and honest reasoning. This is the card of understanding: of the problem solved, the pattern seen, the theory that finally fits the facts. It asks you to examine your assumptions, gather real evidence and let conclusions emerge rather than forcing them. Science in Crowley’s sense is not cold; it is the beauty of a well-ordered mind in which every thread finds its place.
numerology: Six is Tiphareth, the sun-centre of the Tree and the number of harmony; in Air it brings intellect into perfect balance.
affirmation: I look at what is true, think it through, and let understanding guide me.

ctx.past: Careful study, research or a clever solution helped lay the groundwork for where you are now. You learned to look at problems patiently and methodically. That habit of mind is still one of your most reliable resources in this situation.
ctx.present: Your thinking is unusually clear and well ordered at the moment. You can step back from the emotion of the situation and see how its pieces fit together. The heart of the matter is to trust your reasoning and apply it calmly, step by step.
ctx.future: Understanding is on its way. A problem that has puzzled you is likely to yield, perhaps through new information, an expert’s help or a sudden insight. Expect the confusing parts of this situation to start making sense very soon.
ctx.challenge: The shadow of Science is analysis that never stops: treating feelings as data, intellectualising pain or waiting for perfect information before acting. Logic is a fine servant and a poor master. Make sure your head is in conversation with your heart.
ctx.advice: Treat the situation like an experiment. Gather facts, question your assumptions, try a small test and observe the results honestly. Write things down if that helps. Let evidence, rather than fear or wishful thinking, decide your next move.
ctx.self: You are curious, clear-headed and capable of untangling complex things. Your ability to stay objective when others are swept up in drama is a real asset. Trust your intelligence; it is more than equal to what you face.
ctx.others: Others see you as thoughtful, logical and someone whose judgement can be relied on. The environment, too, rewards clear thinking, sound research and new approaches. Ideas offered now are likely to be taken seriously and built upon.
ctx.hopes: You hope to understand, and perhaps fear being out of your depth or fooled. The good news is that your mind is working well. With patience and a methodical approach, what seems murky now will become clear.
ctx.love: In love, this is a meeting of minds. Talking things through, honestly and without blame, brings real understanding between you. Remember to keep warmth in the conversation; being understood and being cherished go hand in hand.
ctx.work: A strong card for research, technology, analysis, teaching and any work that rewards precision. A methodical approach brings success, and innovative ideas can find a workable form. Check the details, then trust the plan you have made.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through understanding. The rose cross at the centre reminds you that knowledge and devotion are not opposites. Study, inquiry and honest reflection can be sacred practices that bring you closer to the truth of things.
ctx.release: Release fuzzy or fearful thinking and the old assumptions that collapse when examined. Let go of conclusions you reached in panic. Fresh, objective eyes on the situation will reveal possibilities that worry had been hiding from you.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be emotional distance. Being clever about a situation can be a way of not feeling it. Ask whether your logic is serving the truth or protecting you from vulnerability you would rather not touch.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a genuine wish to understand. This situation grew from curiosity, questioning and the search for what is really so. Following that thread honestly will lead you to the clarity you are after.
ctx.gift: Your gift is a balanced, brilliant mind. You can bring order to chaos, explain difficult ideas simply and spot solutions others overlook. When you share that clarity generously, it becomes a gift for everyone around you.

name: Seven of Swords
title: Futility
imagery: Six small swords, their hilts marked with the symbols of the planets, point upward against one large central sword whose hilt bears the Sun. The smaller blades crowd and press against the great one. It shows many minor wills and divided intentions contending with a single central purpose, so that the effort as a whole wavers and comes to little.
meaning: Futility is the Moon in Aquarius: the changeable, dreaming Moon in a cool, detached sign. Plans waver, efforts lack conviction, and energy is spent without result. Crowley associated this card with vacillation, a wish to compromise when firmness is needed and a strength that fails to follow through. It is less a punishment than a diagnosis. When the many little wills that pull you in different directions are brought under one central purpose, the Sun sword, effort stops leaking away and becomes effective again.
numerology: Seven is Netzach, the sphere of Venus and feeling; in Air it unsettles the balanced mind of the Six, scattering resolve.
affirmation: I gather my scattered efforts into one clear, wholehearted aim.

ctx.past: In the past, you may have poured effort into something that went nowhere, or wavered at the decisive moment. Perhaps you tried to please too many people at once. That disappointment can teach you how much your energy is worth when it is focused.
ctx.present: Your energy is leaking right now. You may be keeping too many options open, compromising where you should stand firm, or doing things without really believing in them. The heart of the matter is to find your central aim again and commit to it.
ctx.future: If nothing changes, the road ahead holds more effort for little return. Treat this card as an early warning rather than a prophecy. Choose one direction, give it your full heart, and what looked futile can become a genuine achievement.
ctx.challenge: The obstacle is vacillation. Every time you hedge or back away, you lose momentum. You may also be avoiding a confrontation by agreeing to terms that do not serve you. Half-measures feel safer, but here they are the very thing that drains you.
ctx.advice: Decide what truly matters and drop at least one thing that does not. Stop splitting yourself between competing plans. Then follow through, even when it gets uncomfortable. Wholehearted effort on one thing outperforms half-hearted effort on five.
ctx.self: You may feel unsure whether your efforts are worth it, or restless without knowing quite why. Ask yourself honestly what you actually want, beneath obligations and other people’s expectations. That answer is your central sword.
ctx.others: Others may experience you as hard to pin down, saying yes and then drifting away. Or the people around you are themselves scattered, full of plans that never land. Your steady commitment could be the anchor this group needs.
ctx.hopes: You may fear that nothing you do will make a difference, and hope to find work that feels meaningful. Meaning returns when your actions line up with your real purpose. Futility is often just energy pointed in too many directions.
ctx.love: In love, mixed signals and hesitation are causing confusion. Someone may be keeping a foot out of the door or avoiding a necessary conversation. Clarity about what each of you truly wants will do more good than any careful compromise.
ctx.work: At work, projects may stall through unclear priorities or lukewarm commitment. Narrow your focus, finish what matters and decline what does not. A clear goal and consistent follow-through will turn scattered effort into visible progress.
ctx.spirit: Spirit asks you to remember your central sun. When your many small wishes are brought into line with your true Will, the deeper purpose behind your life, effort stops being futile and starts to feel like flow.
ctx.release: Release commitments you keep out of guilt and plans that no longer excite you. Let go of the need to keep everyone happy. Every unnecessary obligation you lay down returns energy to the one thing you most want to do.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the indecision may be fear: if you never fully commit, you can never fully fail. That protection costs more than it saves. The hidden invitation is to risk being wholehearted, and to discover how capable you are when you are.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation lies a divided will, several desires pulling against each other. Until they are named and ranked, effort will keep scattering. Recognising the split inside you is the first step to bringing it together.
ctx.gift: Your gift is versatility: you see many options and can adapt to almost anything. When that flexibility serves a single, clear purpose instead of replacing one, you become remarkably effective and surprisingly hard to stop.

name: Eight of Swords
title: Interference
imagery: Two long, straight swords point downward while six shorter blades of different shapes and cultures, curved and wavy, cross over them. The design feels crowded and tangled against a dim background. The long swords show a clear purpose; the crossing blades show the many small distractions, interruptions and petty obstacles that get in its way.
meaning: Interference is Jupiter in Gemini: the expansive planet scattered by the busy, two-minded sign of the twins. Good intentions are blocked by small things: unexpected hindrances, too much information, second thoughts, other people’s demands. Crowley associated it with a lack of persistence, energy wasted on trifles when it should go to the main purpose. This card asks you to notice exactly what is getting in your way, much of which may be inside your own mind, and to clear it calmly. The two straight swords are still there; your task is to find their line again.
numerology: Eight is Hod, the sphere of Mercury, intellect and detail; in Air it overloads the mind, and thought becomes interference.
affirmation: I clear the clutter from my path and follow my purpose steadily.

ctx.past: In the past, things kept getting in the way: small setbacks, interruptions, other people’s needs or your own second-guessing. The pattern may have left you feeling that progress is always blocked. Seeing that pattern clearly is how you start to break it.
ctx.present: Something is interfering with your progress. It may be red tape, a stream of distractions or your own thoughts going round in circles. The heart of the matter is to identify the real obstacle among all the noise and address it directly.
ctx.future: Delays and minor hindrances may lie ahead, the kind that test your patience more than your strength. They are manageable. Keep returning to your main goal, adapt where you need to, and persistence will carry you through the tangle.
ctx.challenge: The obstacle is overthinking and a scattered focus. You may be giving equal attention to every small problem until none of them gets solved. Too much information, too many opinions and too little follow-through are the crossing blades in your path.
ctx.advice: Simplify. Write down everything that is blocking you, then choose the one or two items that truly matter and deal with them first. Protect your time and attention. Persistence, applied steadily to the main thing, is your way through.
ctx.self: You may feel hemmed in, frustrated or pulled in too many directions at once. Be patient with yourself. Your mind is overloaded, not incapable, and clarity returns as soon as you stop trying to hold everything at the same time.
ctx.others: Other people may be interfering with your plans, often without meaning any harm: requests, opinions, interruptions. Or the whole environment is noisy and fragmented. Kind but firm boundaries will help you protect your focus and your time.
ctx.hopes: You may fear being blocked or trapped indefinitely, and hope for a clear road ahead. Most of what stands in your way is smaller than it feels. Each obstacle you remove makes the path visibly wider.
ctx.love: In love, outside voices, busy schedules or overthinking may be getting between you. Concentrate on what is actually happening in the relationship rather than on imagined problems or others’ opinions. Simple, direct conversation clears a lot of static.
ctx.work: At work, expect paperwork, delays or competing demands to slow things down. Stay calm and organised. Streamline what you can, say no to what is not essential and keep the main project moving a little every day.
ctx.spirit: Spirit asks you to quiet the busy mind. A few minutes of silence, a walk without your phone or a simple meditation can let the inner guidance cut through the interference. The signal is there; the noise just needs turning down.
ctx.release: Release the urge to control every detail and to respond to every demand instantly. Let go of distractions that feel urgent but are not important. Your attention is precious, and freeing it is the first step to moving forward.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be a kind of self-interference. Busyness and complication can be an elegant way of avoiding the real step you are afraid to take. Ask gently whether some of these obstacles are ones you are keeping in place.
ctx.foundation: At the root of this situation is a mind spread too thin, with too many priorities competing for the same energy. Choosing what matters most and letting the rest wait will dissolve a surprising amount of the difficulty.
ctx.gift: Your gift is mental agility. You notice many angles, details and possibilities. When you bring that gift to bear on a single purpose, you can find the clear line through even the most tangled situation.

name: Nine of Swords
title: Cruelty
imagery: Nine jagged swords of uneven length point downward, their blades notched and rusted, dripping blood and poison against a dark, oppressive background. Nothing in the image is at rest. The dripping blades show thoughts turned into weapons, especially against oneself, and the gloom shows a mind lost in fear and despair.
meaning: Cruelty is Mars in Gemini: aggressive Mars in the restless sign of thought and talk. This is the mind at its harshest, full of worry, guilt, self-criticism and the dull cruelty of an intellect cut off from feeling. Crowley saw here the primitive instincts of the psyche at their least enlightened. Yet the card is a mirror rather than a sentence. It shows where your thoughts have become blades, and it invites you to lay them down. Meeting your darkest thoughts with honesty, compassion and support is the beginning of their transformation.
numerology: Nine is Yesod, the foundation and the sphere of the Moon; in Air it raises the hidden fears of the mind to the surface.
affirmation: I meet my harshest thoughts with compassion, and they lose their hold on me.

ctx.past: A period of harshness lies behind you: cruel words from others, or a long stretch of worry and self-blame. Those thoughts may still echo at quiet moments. Naming that past for what it was helps you stop living inside it.
ctx.present: Your mind may be its own harshest critic right now, running through worst-case scenarios and old regrets. Anxiety can feel like truth when it is loud. The heart of the matter is learning to answer that inner voice with kindness rather than agreement.
ctx.future: A stressful stretch may lie ahead, where fears grow louder or someone is unkind. You do not have to meet it alone or unarmed. Support, rest and gentle self-talk will carry you through, and the darkness will pass.
ctx.challenge: The obstacle is self-torment: thoughts that wound instead of guide. You may be punishing yourself for things long past or rehearsing disasters that have not happened. Notice when your mind turns cruel, and refuse to sharpen the blade further.
ctx.advice: Speak to yourself as you would to a frightened friend. Write the fears down so they lose some of their size, and talk to someone you trust. If the weight feels too heavy, reaching out for support is a brave and wise step.
ctx.self: You may be feeling anxious, guilty or worn down by your own thoughts. Be gentle with yourself. These feelings are real, but they are not the whole truth about you, and they are not permanent.
ctx.others: Someone around you may be harsh, critical or careless with their words, or the atmosphere itself feels cold. Protect yourself from absorbing that cruelty. You can hold your boundaries clearly without becoming cruel in return.
ctx.hopes: You may fear that the darkness will never lift, and hope above all for peace of mind. That peace is possible. It usually returns step by step, as you loosen fear’s grip one thought at a time.
ctx.love: In love, harsh words or anxious imaginings may be causing pain. Look honestly at what is real and what is fear talking. Speak kindly, ask directly rather than assume, and protect your heart without letting it harden.
ctx.work: At work, stress, criticism or impossible expectations may be weighing on you. Take your wellbeing seriously. Set limits, take breaks, and remember that no job is worth losing your health or your peace of mind over.
ctx.spirit: Spirit asks you to look your fears in the eye. Shadows shrink when light falls on them. Compassion is the medicine for cruelty, and the compassion you offer yourself is the place where healing begins.
ctx.release: Release self-blame, old guilt and the habit of rehearsing the worst. Let go of the harsh voice that claims to protect you by tormenting you. You can learn from the past without being punished by it forever.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be fears you have not admitted, working quietly beneath the surface and fuelling your anxiety. Bringing them gently into the light, in a journal or a trusted conversation, can begin to take away their sting.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a mind separated from the heart. When thought runs without feeling, it turns cold and cruel. Reconnecting the two, letting your heart have a say in what you think, is what heals the situation.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the courage to face the dark. Having known mental anguish, you understand others’ suffering in a way many cannot. That understanding can make you a deeply compassionate guide for those still finding their way out.

name: Ten of Swords
title: Ruin
imagery: Ten swords are arranged in the pattern of the Tree of Life, their hilts placed at the ten spheres, against a fierce red background. The central sword, at the heart of the Tree, is shattered by the others crowding in on it. The image shows a mental structure pushed past its limit and breaking apart, and with it the ground cleared for something new.
meaning: Ruin is the Sun in Gemini: the light of reason splintered by the divided, restless mind until the old structure can no longer stand. This card describes a complete ending: of a plan, a belief system, a way of living or thinking that has reached its limit. In the Thoth tradition it is not doom but clearance. Reason pushed to its extreme breaks down, and something larger than reason can enter. Let go of what is finished, grieve if you need to, and trust that the cleared ground is where a truer structure can be built.
numerology: Ten is Malkuth, the final sphere and the completion of the suit; in Air it brings mental structures to their end so that the cycle can begin again.
affirmation: I let what has ended fall away, and I build anew on cleared ground.

ctx.past: A collapse lies in your past, a time when a plan, a role or a way of life fell apart. It was painful, and perhaps you still feel its echoes. Yet much of what you are building now could only begin because that old structure came down.
ctx.present: Something has reached its end. A plan, belief or situation can no longer hold together, however hard you try. The heart of the matter is acceptance: the sooner you stop propping up what is falling, the sooner you can turn to what comes next.
ctx.future: A significant ending is coming. It may feel at first like ruin, but it is also a clearing of the ground. Whatever falls away makes room for a better-founded future, and you will be surprised how much lighter you feel afterwards.
ctx.challenge: The challenge is clinging to what has already fallen, or dramatising the collapse until it seems to be the whole of life. Overthinking it will not raise it again. The work here is to let the ending be an ending, without adding more wounds.
ctx.advice: Accept that this chapter is closed. Grieve what deserves grieving, then begin clearing the debris: practical tasks, honest conversations, tidy goodbyes. Then look at what remains standing and ask what you want to build on it.
ctx.self: You may feel exhausted, flattened or at the end of your rope. Be very gentle with yourself. The worst moment of an ending is often the one just before relief begins, and you are closer to that turning point than you think.
ctx.others: Others may see you going through a hard time, or the whole environment may be in upheaval. Lean on people who are kind and honest. Shared endings, faced together, can become the start of stronger alliances.
ctx.hopes: You may fear total collapse and hope, quietly, for a clean slate. Both are held in this card. When a structure falls completely, there is no more need to defend it, and that brings an unexpected freedom.
ctx.love: In love, a relationship, or a pattern within one, may be ending. Let it go with as much dignity and kindness as you can. Whether the bond continues in a new form or closes, what follows can be healthier and truer.
ctx.work: At work, a project, plan or role may collapse. Treat it as a chance to rebuild on firmer foundations and to learn from what did not hold. Practical decisions about money and next steps are best made calmly, with good advice.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through the ending. The Sun still shines in Gemini, even when the swords break: light outlasts every structure the mind builds. Trust the larger cycle of renewal; something within you is being freed by this fall.
ctx.release: Release what is finished: the plan that failed, the belief that no longer fits, the hope you have outgrown. Holding on only prolongs the pain. Let the old swords lie where they fell and walk on.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be a fear of change so strong that you keep rebuilding the very thing that keeps collapsing. Ask yourself what you are clinging to, and whether letting it fall might actually be a relief.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a structure that could not bear any more weight, too rigid, too divided or built on a false premise. Understanding why it fell is the key to building something stronger next time.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the capacity to begin again. You have survived endings before and you will survive this one, wiser and freer. Like the Tree in the card, you can be rebuilt from the ground up, sphere by sphere.

name: Princess of Swords
title: Earth of Air
imagery: A young warrior woman stands amid swirling clouds, her helmet crested with the head of Medusa, and drives her sword downward toward a small, bare altar as smoke billows around her. Her stance is fierce and unafraid. The Medusa helm shows the power to turn illusion to stone, and the downward thrust shows the force of the mind brought down into practical action on earth.
meaning: The Princess of Swords is Earth of Air: the volatile mind made solid, practical and determined. Crowley described her as the wrath of the gods, the force that clears away what is stale, corrupt or outworn so that cleaner forms can appear. She is firm, clever, independent and practical in her handling of problems, though she can be quick to anger and combative. Her energy, rightly used, is constructive: she cuts through confusion and acts. This card asks you to ground your ideas in real deeds and to defend what matters with courage and good sense.
astrology: Earth of Air · rules a quadrant of the heavens around the North Pole (Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces)
numerology: The Princess is the throne of the Ace: the final materialisation of the suit, bringing the force of Air down into the world.
affirmation: I bring my clear mind down to earth in fierce, practical action.

ctx.past: In the past you took a firm, independent stand: you defended your truth, cleared away something stale or refused to accept nonsense. That fierce practicality is part of your foundation, and the space you cleared then is still useful.
ctx.present: The situation calls for you to stop theorising and act. You can see what needs doing; now ground it in practical steps. The heart of the matter is turning clear thought into deeds, and protecting what matters while you do it.
ctx.future: A situation is coming that asks for vigilance and decisive action. You may need to clear away clutter, end a stale arrangement or stand up for what is right. Be ready, and trust your ability to handle it practically.
ctx.challenge: The danger is anger without aim. Righteous indignation can become simple combativeness, and clearing away the old can tip into destroying what was still useful. Before you strike, make sure the target truly deserves the blade.
ctx.advice: Act on your insight. Tackle the practical problem in front of you, declutter your space or your schedule, and make the call you have been putting off. Be brave and direct, and keep both feet on the ground.
ctx.self: You are alert, capable and fiercely independent right now. Trust your instincts and your common sense. Your strength works best when it is guided by wisdom rather than by the heat of the moment. Choose your battles and win them well.
ctx.others: Others may see you as sharp, formidable or a little combative. Or there is someone around you clearing the air with bold, practical action, perhaps upsetting a few people while doing necessary work. Their directness may serve everyone.
ctx.hopes: You hope to make a real difference and may fear being too harsh in the process. Courage and compassion are not enemies. Hold them together and your actions will be both powerful and fair, and people will remember both.
ctx.love: In love, honesty and directness can clear the air of long-standing tension. Say what you mean, practically and plainly, but with care. A down-to-earth approach to shared problems, one concrete step at a time, will move things forward.
ctx.work: At work, practical problem-solving and decisive action pay off. Cut away inefficiency, fix what is broken and handle disputes firmly. This is a time for rolling up your sleeves and doing the job, not endlessly discussing it in meetings.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through the warrior who guards the sacred. Your clear mind can serve something higher when it acts with integrity. Sometimes the holiest thing is to sweep away what is stale so that something living can enter.
ctx.release: Release outworn ideas and arrangements that you keep out of habit. Let go too of the fear of conflict that keeps you from acting, and of anger that serves no constructive end. Clear the ground and keep only what is alive.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be a pleasure in destruction for its own sake, or a defensiveness that strikes before it is struck. Make sure your fierceness is clearing the way for something better, not simply keeping people at a distance.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies the need to bring ideas down to earth. Thought has been circling without landing. Practical, grounded action is what this situation has been waiting for all along, and you are the one who can supply it.
ctx.gift: Your gift is fierce clarity joined to practical sense. You can see through confusion, act on what you see and protect what matters. Few people can both think sharply and act firmly; you can do both, and that makes you a formidable ally.

name: Knight of Swords
title: Fire of Air
imagery: An armoured rider charges headlong through a stormy sky on a galloping horse, sword raised in one hand and dagger in the other. His helmet carries spinning wings like a propeller, and swallows dive around him. The whole image is speed and onrush: the mind in rapid, fiery motion, attacking its goal with fierce and single-minded intent.
meaning: The Knight of Swords is Fire of Air: the fiery, active force of the intellect, the idea at full gallop. Crowley described him as the pure idea of attack, active, clever, skilful and fierce. He can achieve a great deal very quickly and is splendid when a bold stroke is needed. His shadow is impulsiveness: rushing in, overpowering others or charging off before the plan is complete. This card asks you to act decisively while keeping your purpose clearly in sight. Direct his energy well and he will carry you farther and faster than you thought possible.
numerology: The Knight is the fiery, initiating force of the suit, the first lightning rush of its power from the source.
affirmation: I move swiftly toward my goal, my mind clear and my aim true.

ctx.past: Swift, decisive action set things in motion. Perhaps you charged ahead toward a goal, made a bold move or cut a situation short. The energy of that charge still drives events, for better or worse, and much of the present follows from it.
ctx.present: The moment calls for decisive movement. Hesitation will cost more than a well-aimed risk. The heart of the matter is to act with speed and focus, keeping your mind as sharp as your intention and your eyes on the target.
ctx.future: Rapid developments are coming: news, an opportunity or a challenge that arrives at full speed. Be ready to respond quickly. Keep your purpose in mind so that this sudden energy carries you forward rather than scattering you.
ctx.challenge: The obstacle is impetuousness. Charging ahead without listening, overriding others or acting before the plan is ready can cause damage you then have to repair. Speed is a gift only when it serves a clear aim.
ctx.advice: Move now. Make the call, send the proposal, take the bold step you have been thinking about. Focus your energy on one target and go for it, but glance at the map now and then to be sure you are still heading where you mean to go.
ctx.self: You are driven, focused and ready for action. Your mind is quick and your will is strong. Trust that energy, and remember that pausing to check your direction is not the same as losing momentum.
ctx.others: Others may see you as ambitious, intense or a little overwhelming. Or someone around you is charging in with fierce ideas and plenty of force. Their speed can be useful, provided someone keeps an eye on the details.
ctx.hopes: You may hope to achieve something quickly and fear losing control along the way. Both are understandable with this much energy in play. Balance pace with judgement and you can have both speed and safety on this ride.
ctx.love: In love, feelings are expressed boldly and directly. Passion and honesty can sweep things forward fast. Make sure you are listening as well as declaring, so that the other person has room to keep pace with you.
ctx.work: At work, swift action and sharp focus bring results. It is a strong time to push a project forward, pitch an idea or tackle a problem head-on. Back up your boldness with solid preparation and you will be hard to beat.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through Will in motion. When your actions are aligned with your true purpose, they gather a momentum that seems to carry you. Let the Knight’s fire serve what you most deeply intend, and it will not burn out.
ctx.release: Release the hesitation that keeps you waiting for perfect conditions. Release, too, any recklessness that throws energy at everything at once. Keep the speed and the courage, but drop the scatter. One well-aimed charge achieves more than a dozen wild ones.
ctx.shadow: Beneath the rush may be a restlessness that avoids sitting still with uncomfortable thoughts or feelings. Constant motion can be a way of not reflecting. Make some quiet time to think as well as act.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a fierce drive toward a particular goal. This situation was set in motion by ambition and the desire to make something happen. Understanding where that drive comes from helps you direct it wisely.
ctx.gift: Your gift is the ability to act decisively and fast. When others are still deliberating, you can see the opening and take it. That courage to move is a real strength in any situation that needs breaking open.

name: Queen of Swords
title: Water of Air
imagery: A crowned queen sits enthroned on clouds in a sky of crystalline light, her helmet crested with the head of a child. In one hand she raises a sword, and in the other she holds the severed head of a bearded man. The severed head shows the cutting away of illusion and false authority, the child’s head the clear, innocent perception that remains once the mind is freed.
meaning: The Queen of Swords is Water of Air: the receptive, reflective side of the mind, the clear mirror of thought. She perceives keenly, judges fairly and sees straight through pretence. In Crowley’s description she is the liberator of the mind, cutting away the false ideas and conditioned beliefs that bind us. She is graceful, confident and independent, sometimes cool, and honest to the point of severity. This card asks you to see things as they truly are and to speak with clarity and integrity. Her coolness is not coldness but the calm of a mind set free.
numerology: The Queen is the receptive, reflective force of the suit, who gives form to the Knight’s fiery impulse.
affirmation: I see clearly, speak truly and free my mind from every illusion.

ctx.past: In the past, clear perception served you well. You saw through a pretence, made a fair judgement or spoke a hard truth that needed saying. That act of clarity freed you from something, and it is part of the ground you stand on now.
ctx.present: The situation calls for clear eyes. Strip away assumptions, flattery and wishful thinking and look at what is actually in front of you. The heart of the matter is perception: once you see it truly, you will know what to do.
ctx.future: Clarity and release are coming. An illusion is about to fall away, perhaps about a person, a plan or your own story. It may feel sharp at first, but you will find yourself lighter and freer once you can see things as they are.
ctx.challenge: The shadow here is severity. Clear judgement without compassion can become cutting, critical or cold. Be careful that your honesty does not become a weapon, and that your independence does not quietly turn into isolation.
ctx.advice: Tell the truth, starting with yourself. Name what you see without exaggeration or apology. Cut away the beliefs and obligations that are not really yours. A calm, honest word now is worth more than a hundred careful evasions.
ctx.self: You are perceptive, independent and difficult to fool. Trust your reading of the situation. Let your clarity be graceful rather than harsh, and you will find people value your insight even when it is not what they hoped to hear.
ctx.others: Others see you as clear-sighted, fair and perhaps a little reserved. Or there is someone near you, often a woman of experience, who offers honest, perceptive counsel. Their words may be cool, but they come from a genuine wish to help.
ctx.hopes: You may hope to know the truth and fear what it will reveal. Clarity can sting, yet it is always freeing in the end. Whatever you discover, you will be better placed to choose once you know it.
ctx.love: In love, honesty and real seeing matter most. See the other person as they truly are, not as you wish they were, and let yourself be seen. Speak clearly about your needs and boundaries, with warmth as well as candour.
ctx.work: At work, perceptive analysis and fair judgement bring success. This favours evaluation, editing, negotiation and any role that requires discernment. Give honest, constructive feedback, and accept it in the same spirit. Clear contracts and clear expectations will save trouble later.
ctx.spirit: Spirit speaks through liberation. When your mind is freed from inherited illusions and borrowed beliefs, you can perceive your own true nature. Every false idea you cut away brings you closer to that clear, childlike seeing.
ctx.release: Release illusions, comforting lies and beliefs you took on without examining them. Let go of anything that clouds your perception, including other people’s opinions of who you should be. What remains when the fog lifts is your own clear sight.
ctx.shadow: The hidden side may be emotional detachment. Clarity can become a safe place from which to judge without feeling. Make sure your sharp eyes are also willing to look honestly and kindly at your own heart.
ctx.foundation: At the root lies a wish for truth, perhaps after a long time of being misled or misleading yourself. That desire for clarity, and for freedom from what has been false, is the force behind this whole situation.
ctx.gift: Your gift is clear perception. You can see through pretence, judge fairly and help others discover what is real. That clarity, offered with grace and warmth, can free not only you but many of the people around you.

name: Prince of Swords
title: Air of Air
imagery: A young man rides a chariot drawn by small winged children who pull in different directions as they please, so that the chariot lurches rather than glides. He holds a sword in one hand to create and a sickle in the other to cut down what he has made, surrounded by geometric shapes and swirling air. The image shows pure intellect: endlessly inventive, endlessly dismantling, and not always steering.
meaning: The Prince of Swords is Air of Air: the mind in its purest, most airy form. He is full of ideas, theories, plans and designs, creating them with one hand and cutting them down with the other. Crowley described him as purely intellectual, clever and full of brilliant ideas, but also unstable and changeable, since his chariot horses pull in any direction. His genius is real, yet ideas need a direction to become real. This card asks you to use your intelligence creatively while anchoring it in purpose. When the mind serves the Will, it becomes a superb instrument of creation.
numerology: The Prince is the son of the Knight and the Queen, the force of the suit carried out into action and expression.
affirmation: My mind is a creative force, and I give it a clear direction.

ctx.past: A season of ideas, plans and theories shaped where you are now. You may have explored many possibilities, perhaps creating and abandoning several. Those intellectual adventures left you with knowledge and perspective you can draw on.
